zh: 让我单摆浮搁的讲一套北平，我没办法。
en:
But I shall be at a complete loss
if I should be called upon
to write exclusively about Peiping.N

zh: 北平的地方那么大，事情那么多，我知道的真觉太少了，虽然我生在那里，一直到廿七岁才离开。
en:
Peiping is so big and multifaceted
that very little of it, I believe,
is known to me
though I was born and brought up there
and never went away until I was 27.

zh: 以名胜说，我没到过陶然亭，这多可笑！
en:
Just fancy that
I have neglected to visit even Tao Tan Ting,
a local scenic attraction!

zh: 以此类推，我所知道的那点只是“我的北平”，而我的北平大概等于牛的一毛。
en:
It follows that,
in contrast with Peiping in its entirety,
what little I know about it
is probably a mere drop in the ocean.

zh:
可是，我真爱北平。
这个爱几乎是要说而说不出的。
我爱我的母亲。怎样爱？我说不出。
en:
I do cherish, however,
a genuine love for Peiping
——a love that is almost
as inexpressible as my love for mother.

zh: 在我想作一件事讨她老人家喜欢的时候，我独自微微的笑着；在我想到她的健康而不放心的时候，我欲落泪。
en:
I smile by myself
when I think of something
I can do to please mother;
I feel like crying
when I worry about mother's health.

zh: 言语是不够表现我的心情的，只有独自微笑或落泪才足以把内心揭露在外面一些来。
en:
Words fail me
where silent smiles and tears well
express my innermost feelings.

zh:
我之爱北平也近乎这个。
夸奖这个古城的某一点是容易的，可是那就把北平看得太小了。
en:
The same is true of my love for Peiping.
I shall fail to do justice
to this vast ancient city
if I should do no more than
extol just one certain aspect of it.

zh: 我所爱的北平不是枝枝节节的一些什么，而是整个儿与我的心灵相粘合的一段历史，一大块地方，
en:
The Peiping I love is not
something in bits and pieces,
but a phase of history
and a vast tract of land
completely bound up with my heart.

zh: 多少风景名胜，从雨后什刹海的蜻蜓一直到我梦里的玉泉山的塔影，都积凑到一块，
en:
Numerous scenic spots and historical sites
from Shi Sha Hai Lake
with its dragonflies after a rain
to the Yu Quan Shan Mountain
with the dream pagoda on top
——all merge into a single whole.

zh: 每一小的事件中有个我，我的每一思念中有个北平，这只有说不出而已。
en:
I associate myself with everything in Peiping
no matter how trivial it is;
Peiping is always in my mind.
I can't tell why.

zh: 真愿成为诗人，把一切好听好看的字都浸在自己的心血里，像杜鹃似的啼出北平的俊伟。
en:
If only I were a poet so that,
with all the sweet and beautiful words
at my command,
I would sing of the grandeur of Peiping in
as longing a note as that of a cuckoo!

zh: 啊！我不是诗人！我将永远道不出我的爱，一种像由音乐与图画所引起的爱。
en:
Alas, I am no poet!
I shall never be able to express my love
——the kind of love
as inspired by music or painting.

zh:
这不但是辜负了北平，也对不住我自己，
因为我是最初的知识与印象都得自北平，它是在我的血里，我的性格与脾气里有许多地方是这古城所赐给的。
en:
That is quite a letdown
to both Peiping and myself,
for it is to this ancient city
that I owe what I have within me,
including my early knowledge and impressions
as well as much of
my character and temperament.

zh: 我不能爱上海与天津，因为我心中有个北平。可是我说不出来！
en:
With Peiping possessing my heart,
I can never
become attached to either Shanghai or Tianjin.
I can't tell why.

zh: 伦敦，巴黎，罗马与堪司坦丁堡，曾被称为欧洲的四大“历史的都城”。
en:
London, Paris, Rome and Constantinople
are known as
the four major "historic capitals"of Europe.

zh: 我知道一些伦敦的情形；巴黎与罗马只是到过而已；堪司坦丁堡根本没有去过。

就伦敦，巴黎，罗马来说，巴黎更近似北平
——虽然“近似”两字都拉扯得很远过，假使让我“家住巴黎”，我一定会和没有家一样的感到寂苦。
en:
Of all these cities,
Paris has the closest affinity with Peiping
(The word"affinity"
may perhaps sound a bit farfetched).
Nevertheless, if should make my home in Paris,
I would feel very lonely
as if I had no home at all.

zh:
巴黎，据我看，(表观点的词语提前）还太热闹。
自然，那里也有空旷静寂的地方，可是又未免太旷；
en:
As far as I know,
Paris is too much of a bustling town.
It does have quiet open spaces,
but they smack of mere expanses of vacancy.

zh: 不像北平那样复杂而又有个边际，使我能摸着——那长着红酸枣的老城墙！
en:
Peiping is complicated and yet tangible.
I can feel it by touch.
I can feel the red wild jujubes
growing on its ancient city wall!

zh: 面向着积水滩，背后是城墙，坐在石上看水中的小蝌蚪或苇叶上的嫩蜻蜓，我可以快乐的坐一天，心中完全安适，无所求也无可怕，像小儿安睡在摇篮里
en:
I can spend a whole day enjoying myself
sitting on a rock to observe
tiny tadpoles in the water
or tender dragonflies on reeds
while facing me lies Ji Shui Tan Pond
and right behind me rises the high city wall.
I can thus enjoy a perfect inner clam,
free from any desire or fear,
like a child sleeping peacefully in the cradle.

zh: 是的，北平也有热闹的地方，但是它和太极拳相似，动中有静。
en:
There are also bustling places in Peiping,
to be sure, but like
the traditional Chinese shadow boxing
Tai Ji Quan,
the city retains its stillness
in the midst of motion.

zh: 巴黎有许多地方使人疲乏，所以咖啡与酒是必要的，以便刺激；在北平，有温和的香片茶就够了。
en:
While Parisians have to turn to
coffee or wine for the relief of boredom
caused by so many wearisome places in their city,
the mild beverage of jasmine tea
will be more than adequate for dwellers of Peiping.

zh: 论说巴黎的布置已比伦敦罗马匀调的多了，可是比上北平还差点事儿。
en:
Though Paris has a better layout
than London or Rome,
it nevertheless cannot compare with Peiping,

zh: 北平在人为之中显出自然，几乎是什么地方即不挤得慌，又不太僻静；最小的胡同里的房子也有院子与树；最空旷的地方也离买卖街与住宅区不远。
en:
one always finds the natural
in the midst of the artificial.
The city as a whole is
neither too crowded nor too secluded.
Even houses tucked away
in very small lanes
have their own courtyards and trees.
Even the most secluded places
are situated within
a stone's throw of business or residential districts.

zh: 这种配法可以算——在我的经验中——天下第一了。
en:
Such a layout is,
to my mind,
without equal all over the world.

zh: 北平的好处不在处处设备得完全，而在它处处有空儿，可以使我自由的喘气；不在有好些美丽的建筑，而在建筑的四周都有空闲的地方，使它们成为美景。
en:
However, what distinguishes Peiping
is not the perfect layout,
but the open spaces here and there
where people can breathe freely;
not the many beautiful buildings,
but the open grounds around each building
which add to its architectural beauty.

zh: 每一城楼，每一牌楼，都可以从老远就看见。况且在街上还可以看见北山与西山呢！
en:
Each gate tower of the city wall
and each pailou (decorated archway)
can been seen from afar.
And the Northern and Western hills
are visible to people in the open streets.

zh: 好学的，爱古物的，人们自然喜欢北平，因为这里书多古物多。
en:
Those who are fond of
studying or collecting curios
will naturally be drawn to Peiping,
which is remarkable for
its rich store of books and curios.

zh: 我不好学，也没钱买古物。对于物质上，我却喜欢北平的花多菜多果子多。
en:
Personally I am not given to studying,
nor do I have spare money to buy curios.
But I am keen on the flowers, vegetables and fruit
which grow in rich abundance in Peiping.

zh: 花草是种费钱的玩艺，可是此地的“草花儿”很便宜，而且家家有院子，可以花不多的钱而种一院子花，即使算不了什么，可是到底可爱呀。
en:
Gardening is something very expensive.
But since flowers of herbaceous plants
in Peiping are very cheap
and each house has a courtyard of its own,
it does not cost very much
to plant a whole courtyard
to such flowers which, though humble,
are nevertheless lovely to look at,

zh: 墙上的牵牛，墙根的靠山竹与草茉莉，是多么省钱省事而足以招来蝴蝶呀！
en:
such as morning glories on the wall,
china pinks at the foot of wall
and marvels-of-Peru.
Yes, cheap as they are,
they attract butterflies!

zh: 至于青菜，白菜，扁豆，毛豆角，黄瓜，菠菜等等，大多数是直接由城外担来而送到家门口的。
en:
Green vegetables, cabbages,
hyacinth beans, young soya beans,
cucumbers, spinach, etc.
are often carried straight form the suburbs
to your residential quarters for marketing.

zh: 雨后，韭菜叶上还往往带着雨时溅起的泥点，青菜摊子上的红红绿绿几乎有诗似的美丽。
en:
Often, leeks from rural farms after a rain
still have specks of mud on their leaves.
The vegetables stalls are so colorful
that they present a scene of poetic charm.

zh:
果子有不少是由西山与北山来的，
西山的沙果，海棠，北山的黑枣，柿子，进了城还带着一层白霜儿呀！
en:
Fruits come mainly from
the western and northern suburbs,
such as crab apples and cherry apples (地点）
from the Western Hills.
and jujubes and persimmons (地点）
from the Northern Hills.
Look, how they are still covered with frostlike bloom when they are put on the market!

zh: 哼，美国的橘子包着纸，遇到北平的带着霜儿的玉李，还不愧杀！
en:
Indeed, America's paper-wrapped oranges
will pale beside Peiping's plums
bearing a thin coating of frostlike bloom!

zh: 是的，北平是个都城，而能有好多自己产生的花，菜，水果，|这就使人更接近了自然。
en:
The city of Peiping brings its residents
into closer contact with nature
by growing flowers, vegetables and fruit
in large quantities.

zh: 从它里面说，它没有像伦敦的那些成天冒烟的工厂；从外面说，它紧连着园林、菜圃与农村。
en:
The city proper is not plagued by factory chimneys
such as you find in London
giving off volumes of smoke all day long.
On the outskirts of the city
lie numerous flower gardens,
vegetables farms and villages.

zh: 采菊东篱下，在这里，确是可以悠然见南山的；
en:
An ancient Chinese poet
by the name of Tao Yuanming
says aptly in one of his famous poems,"
Plucking chrysanthemums
under the eastern hedge,
I calmly view the southern hills."

zh: 大概把“南”字变个“西”或“北”，也没有多少了不得吧。
en:
To adapt it to life in Peiping,
I might as well
substitute the word"western"or"northern"
for the word "southern" in the line.

zh: 像我这样的一个贫寒的人，或者只有在北平能享受一点清福了。
en:
Peiping is probably the only place
for a man of limited means like me
to live an easy and carefree life in.

zh: 好，不再说了吧；要落泪了，真想念北平呀！
en:
Now, let me leave off writing,
for I am on the point of shedding tears.
How I miss Peiping.

zh: 设若让我写一本小说，以北平作背景，我不至于害怕，因为我可以拣着我知道的写，而躲开我所不知道的。
en:
I have no misgivings about writing a novel
with Peiping as its background
because I can choose to write about
what I am most familiar with
while shying away from
what is less known to me.

zh: 这一次的旅行使我更了解一个名词的意义，这个名词就是：朋友。
en:
On my recent travels,
I came to realize still more fully
the significance of the word "friend".

zh:
七八天以前我曾对一个初次见面的朋友说：
“在朋友们面前我只感到惭愧。你们待我太好了，我简直没法报答你们。”
en:
Seven or eight days ago,
I said to a friend whom I had just come to know,
"I can't help feeling embarrassed before my friends.
You're all so nice to me.
I simply don't know
how to repay your kindness."

zh: 这并不是谦虚的客气话，这是真的事实。
en:
I did not make this remark
out of mere modesty and courtesy.
I truly meant what I said.

zh:
说过这些话，我第二天就离开了那个朋友，并不知道以后还有没有机会再看见他。
但是他给我的那一点点温暖至今还使我的心颤动。
en:
The next day, I said goodbye to this friend,
not knowing if I could ever see him again.
But the little warmth that he gave me has been keeping my heart
throbbing with gratitude.

zh: 我的生命大概不会很长久罢。
en: The length of my days will not be unlimited.

zh:
然而在短促的过去的回顾中却有一盏明灯，
照彻（=照亮）了我的灵魂的黑暗，使我的生存有一点光彩。
en:
However, whenever
I look back on my brief past life,
I find a beacon illuminating my soul
and thereby lending a little brightness to my being.

zh:
这盏灯就是就友情。
我应该感谢它，因为靠了它我才能够活到现在；而且把旧家庭给我留下的阴影扫除了的也正是它。
en:
That beacon is friendship.
I should be grateful to it
because it has helped me keep alive up to now
and clear away the shadow
left on me by my old family.

zh:
世间有不少的人为了家庭抛弃朋友，
至少也会在家庭和朋友之间划一个界限，把家庭看得比朋友重过若干倍。
en:
Many people forsake their friends
in favour of their own families,
or at least draw a line of demarcation
between families and friends,
considering the former to be many times
more important than the latter.

zh:
这似乎是很自然的事情。
我也曾亲眼看见一些人结婚以后就离开朋友，离开事业......
en:
That seems to be a matter of course.
I have also seen with my own eyes
how some people abandon their friends
as well as their own careers
soon after they get married...

zh: 朋友是暂时的，家庭是永久的。在好些人的行为里我发见了这个信条。这个信条在我实在是不可理解的。
en:
Friends are transient
whereas family are lasting
——that is the tenet, as I know,
guiding the behaviour of many people.
To me, that is utterly inconceivable.

zh: 对于我，要是没有朋友，我现在会变成怎样可怜的东西，我自己也不知道。
en:
Without friends,
I would have been reduced to
I don't know what a miserable creature.

zh: 然而朋友们把我救了。他们给了我家庭所不能给的东西。
en:
Friends are my saviours.
They give me things
which it is beyond my family to give me.

zh:
他们的友爱，他们的帮助，他们的鼓励，(1+1=2)
几次把我从深渊的边沿救回来。
en:
Thanks to their fraternal love,
assistance and encouragement,
I have time and again been saved
from falling into an abyss
while on its verge.

zh: 他们对我表示了无限的慷慨。
en: They have been enormously generous towards me.

zh: 我的生活曾经是悲苦的，黑暗的。
en:
There was a time
when my life was miserable and gloomy.

zh: 然而朋友们把多量的同情，多量的爱，多量的欢乐，多量的眼泪分了给我，这些东西都是生存所必需的。
en:
My friends then gave me
in large quantities sympathy, love, joy and tears
——things essential for existence.

zh: 这些不要报答的慷慨的施舍，使我的生活里也有了温暖，有了幸福。
en:
It is due to their bountiful free gifts
that I also have my share of
warmth and happiness in my life.

zh:
我默默地接受了它们。
我并不曾说一句感激的话，我也没有做过一件报答的行为。
en:
I accepted their kindnesses quietly
without ever saying a word of thanks
and without ever doing anything in return.

zh: 但是朋友们却不把自私的形容词加到我的身上。对于我，他们太慷慨了。
en:
In spite of that,
my friends never used
the epithet "self-centered"
when referred to me.
They are only too generous towards me.

zh: 这一次我走了许多新地方，看见了许多新朋友。
en:
I visited many new places
and met new friends on my recent trip.

zh: 我的生活是忙碌的：忙着看，忙着听，忙着说，忙着走。但是我不曾遇到一点困难，朋友们给我准备好了一切，使我不会缺少什么。
en:
My time was mostly taken up by
looking around, listening, talking and walking.
But I never ran into any trouble
because my friends had done their utmost
to make sure that
I would be short of nothing.

zh: 我每走到一个新地方，我就像回到我那个在上海被日本兵毁掉的旧居一样。
en:
Whatever new places I called at,
I always felt at home
as if I were back in my old residence in Shanghai
which had already been raged to the ground
by Japanese troops.

zh: 每一个朋友，不管他自己的生活是怎样苦，怎样简单，也要慷慨地分一些东西给我，虽然明知道我不能够报答他。
en:
No matter how hard up and frugal
my friends themselves were,
they would unstintingly share with me
whatever they had,
although they knew I would not be able to
repay them for their kindness.

zh: 有些朋友，连他们的名字我以前也不知道，他们却关心我的健康，处处打听我的“病况”，
en:
Some, whom I did not even know by name,
showed concern over my health
and went about inquiring after me.

zh: 直到他们看见了我那被日光晒黑了的脸和膀子，他们才放心地微笑了，这种情形的确值得人掉泪。
en:
It was not until
they saw my suntanned face and arms that
they began to smile a smile of relief.
All that was enough to move one to tears.

zh: 有人相信我不写文章就不能够生活。
en:
Some people believe that,
without writing,
I would lose my livelihood.

zh: 两个月以前，一个同情我的上海朋友寄稿到《广州民国日报》的副刊，说了许多关于我的生活的话。
en:
One of my sympathizers,
in an article published two months ago
in the Guangzhou Republic Daily Supplement,
gives a full account of the conditions of my life.

zh: 他也说我一天不写文章第二天就没有饭吃。这是不确实的。
en:
He also says that
I would have nothing to live on
once I should lay down my pen.
That is not true at all.

zh: 这次旅行就给我证明；即使我不再写一个字，朋友们也不肯让我冻馁。
en:
It has already been proved by recent travels
that my friends would never let me
suffer from cold and hunger
even if I should go without writing a single word.

zh: 世间还有许多慷慨的人，他们并不把自己个人和家庭看得异常重要，超过一切。
en:
There are a great many
kind-hearted people in the world
who never attach undue importance
to themselves and their own families
and who never place themselves and their families
above anything else.

zh: 靠了他们我才能够活到现在，而且靠了他们我还要活下去。
en:
It is owing to them that
I still survive
and shall continue to survive
for a long time to come.

zh:
朋友们给我的东西是太多、太多了。
我将怎样报答他们呢？但是我知道他们是不需要报答的。
en:
I owe my friends many, many kindnesses.
How can I repay them?
But, I understand,
they don't need me to do that.

zh: 最近我在一个法国哲学家的书里读到了这样的话：
en:
Recently I came across
the following words in a book
by a French philosopher:

zh: “生命的一个条件就是消费……世间有一种不能跟生存分开的慷慨，要是没有了它，我们就会死，就会丛内部干枯。我们必须开花。道德，无私心就是人生的花。”
en:
One condition of life is consumption...
Survival in this world
is inseparable from generosity,
without which we would perish
and become dried-up from within.
We must put forth flowers.
Moral integrity and unselfishness
are the flowers of life.

zh: 在我的眼前开放着这么多的人生的花朵了。我的生命要到什么时候才会开花？难道我已经是“内部干枯”了吗？(简单句简单译，不要想太多~)
en:
Now so many flowers of life
are in full bloom before my eyes.
When can my life put forth flowers?
Am I already dried-up from within?

zh: 一个朋友说过：“我若是灯，我就要用我的光明来照彻黑暗。”
en:
A friend of mine says,
"If I were a lamp,
I would illuminate darkness
with my light."

zh: 我不配做一盏明灯。那么就让我做一块木柴罢。我愿意把我从太阳那里受到的热放散出来，我愿意把自己烧得粉身碎骨给人间添一点点温暖。
en:
I, however, don't qualify for a bright lamp.
Let me be a piece of firewood instead.
I'll radiate the heat
that I have absorbed from the sun.
I'll burn myself to ashes
to provide this human world with a little warmth.

zh:
一个年轻的朋友写信问我：
“应该做一个什么样的人？”我回答他：“做一个战士。”
en:
A young friend of mine
asked me in a letter,
" What kind of man should I be?"
My answer was,"Be a fighter."

zh: 另一个朋友问我：“怎样对付生活？”我仍旧答道：“做一个战士。”《战士颂》的作者曾经写过这样的话：
en:
Another friend of mine inquired,
"How should I live my life?"
Again my answer was,"Be a fighter."
The author of In Praise of the Fighter says:

zh:
“我激荡在这绵绵不息、涪沱四方的生命洪流中，
我就应该追逐这洪流，而且追过它，自己去造更广、更深的洪流。”
en:
Riding on the ceaseless rushing torrent of life,
I should pursue and overtake it
so as to create
an even greater and deeper torrent of my own.

zh:
“我如果是一盏灯，这灯的用处便是照彻那多量黑暗。
我如果是海潮，便要鼓起波涛去洗涤海边一切陈腐的积物。”
en:
If I were a lamp.
it would be my duty
to light up thick darkness.
If I were the sea tide,
I would marshal rolling waves
to cleanse the beach of all accumulated filth.

zh: 这一段话很恰当地写出了战士的心情。在这个时代，战士是最需要的。
en:
This quotation reflects aptly
the state of mind of a fighter.
Fighters are badly needed in our time.

zh:
但是这样的战士并不一定要持枪上战场。
(+除了子弹，)他的武器还可以是知识、信仰和坚强的意志。
en:
But such fighters do not necessarily
go to the battlefield gun in hand.
Their weapons are not necessarily bullets.
Their weapons may be
knowledge, faith and strong will.

zh: 他并不一定要流仇敌的血，却能更有把握地致敌人的死命。
en: They can bring the enemy sure death without drawing his blood.

zh: 战士是永远追求光明的。
en: A fighter is always in pursuit of light.

zh:
他并不躺在晴空下享受阳光，
却在暗夜里燃起火炬，给人们照亮道路，使他们走向黎明。
en:
Instead of basking in the sunshine under a clear sky,
he holds a burning torch in the darkness of night
to illuminate people's way
so that they can continue their journey
till they see the dawn of a new day.

zh: 驱散黑暗，这是战士的任务。
en: It is the task of a fighter to dispel darkness.

zh: 他不躲避黑暗，却要面对黑暗，跟躲藏在阴影里的魅魅、胭陋搏斗。
en:
Instead of shirking darkness,
he braves it
and fights the hidden demons and monsters therein.

zh:
他要消灭它们而取得光明。
战士是不知道妥协的。
他得不到光明便不会停止战斗。
en: He is determined to wipe them out and win light.

zh: 战士是永远年轻的，他不犹豫，不休息。
en:
A fighter is perennially young.
He is never irresolute or inactive.

zh: 他深入人丛中，找寻苍蝇、毒蚊等等危害人类的东西（7)
en:
He plunges deep into teeming crowds
in search of such vermin
as flies and venomous mosquitoes.

zh: 他不断地攻击它们，不肯与它们共同生存在一个天空下面。
en:
He will fight them relentlessly
and refuse to coexist with them
under the same sky.

zh: 对于战士，生活就是不停的战斗。
en:
To him,
life means nothing
but continuous fighting.

zh: 他不是取得光明而生存，便是带着满身伤痕而死去。在战斗中力量只有增长，信仰只有加强。
en:
He either survives by winning light,
or perishes with his body covered
all over with cuts and bruises.
Fighting just serves to
increase his stamina
and strengthen his faith.

zh: 在战斗中给战士指路的是“未来”，“未来”给人以希望和鼓舞。
en:
In the course of the struggle,
it is the "future" that serves as
the beacon light to him;
the "future" gives people hope and inspiration.

zh: 战士永远不会失去青春的活力。
en: He will never lose his youthful vigour.

zh: 战士是不知道灰心与绝望的。
en: A fighter will never lose heart or despair.

zh: 他甚至在失败的废墟上，还要堆起破碎的砖石重建九级宝塔。
en:
He will pile up broken pieces of brick and stone
to rebuilt a nine-story pagoda on the ruins of failure.

zh: 任何打击都不能击破战士的意志。
en: No blows will ever break his will.

zh: 战士是不知道畏缩的。他的脚步很坚定。
en:
A fighter is always fearless.
His steps are firm.

zh: 他（+一旦）看定目标，便一直向前走去。——→（意合）
en:
Once he has settled on an objective,
he will press right ahead.
→（形合）

zh: 他不怕被绊脚石摔倒，没有一种障碍能使他改变心思。
en:
He is never afraid of
being tripped by a stumbling block.
No obstacles will ever
make him change his mind.

zh: 假象绝不能迷住战士的眼睛，支配战士的行动的是信仰。
en:
His eyes will never
be hoodwinked by false appearance.
His actions are guided by faith.

zh: 他能够忍受一切艰难、痛苦，而达到他所选择的目标。
en:
He can endure any hardships or sufferings
while striving to attain his chosen objective.

zh:
除非他死，人不能使他放弃工作。
这便是我们现在需要的战士。
en:
He will never abandon work
as long as he is alive.
This is the kind of fighter we now need.

zh: 这样的战士并不一定具有超人的能力。
en:
He is not necessarily possessed of
superhuman capability.

zh: 他是一个平凡的人。
en: He is just an ordinary person.

zh: 每个人都可以做战士，只要他有决心。
en:
Anyone can be fighter
so long as he has the determination.

zh: 所以我用“做一个战士”的话来激励那些在彷徨、苦闷中的年轻朋友。
en:
Hence a few words of mine about
" being a fighter"
to encourage those young people
who wander about in a depressed state,
not knowing which way to go.

zh: 我有我的梦中世界，在那里我常常见到你。
en:
I dream my own dream,
in which I often meet you.

zh: 昨夜又见到你那慈祥的笑容了
en:
Last night
I again saw your kindly smiling face.

zh: 还是在我们那个老家，在你的房间里，在我的房间里，你亲切地对我讲话。你笑，我也笑。
en:
It was the same old home of ours.
You talked to me cordially
now in your room, now in my room.
You smiled and I also smiled.

zh: 还是成都的那些旧街道，我跟着你一步一步地走过平坦的石板路，
en:
It was the same old streets of Chengdu.
I followed you step by step
on the smooth flagstones.

zh: 我望着你的背影，心里安慰地想：父亲还很康健呢。一种幸福的感觉使我的全身发热了。
en:
Looking at you from behind,
I inwardly consoled myself with the thought
that father was still hale and hearty.
A sensation of blissfulness
warmed me up all over.

zh: 我那时不会知道我是在梦中，也忘记了二十五年来的艰苦日子。
en:
was unaware that I was in a dream.
I also forgot
the hardships I had gone through
during the past 25 years.

zh: 在戏园里，我坐在你旁边，看台上的武戏，你还详细地给我解释剧中情节。
en:
While I sat beside you inside a theater
watching the fighting scenes of Peking opera,
you explained its story to me in great detail.

zh:
我变成二十几年前的孩子了。
我高兴，我没有挂虑地微笑，我不假思索地随口讲话。
我想不到/我在很短的时间以后/就会/失掉你，失掉这一切。
en:
I was again the small kid of 25 years before.
I was joyful, I smiles,
I chattered away freely.
I did not have the slightest inkling
that you together with everything else
would in a moment vanish out of sight.

zh: 然而睁开眼睛，我只是一个人，(主废关系）四周就只有滴滴的雨声。房里是一片黑暗。
en:
When I opened my eyes,
I found that I was all by myself
and nothing was heard
except the pit-a-pat of rain drops.

zh: 没有笑，没有话语。只有雨声：滴—滴—滴。
en:
No more smile, no more chitchat.
Only the drip drip drip of rain.

zh: 我用力把眼睛睁大，我擦开蚊帐，我在漆黑的空间中找寻你影子。
en:
Forcing my eyes to open wider
and drawing aside the mosquito net,
I began to search for you
in the pitch darkness.

zh: 但是从两扇开着的小窗，慢慢地透进来灰白色的亮光，使我的眼睛看见了这个空阔的房间。
en:
A greyish light, nevertheless,
edged in through two small windows
to enable me to see the spacious room.

zh: 没有你，没有你的微笑。有的是寂寞、单调。雨一直滴—滴地下着。
en:
You and your smile were no more.
Only loneliness and monotony remained.
The rain kept pitter-pattering.

zh:
我唤你，没有回应。
我侧耳倾听，没有脚声。
我静下来，我的心怦怦地跳动。
我听见自己的心的声音。
en:
I called to you, but no response.
I listened attentively, but heard no footsteps.
I quieted down, my heart beating hard.
I could hear its thumping.

zh: 我的心在走路，它慢慢地走过了二十五年，一直到这个夜晚。
en:
My heart had been
tramping along all the time.
Up to now,
it had been on its slow journey for 25 years.

zh:
我于是闭了嘴，我知道你不会再站到我的面前。
二十五年前我失掉了你。我从无父的孩子已经长成一个中年人了。
en:
Thereupon I kept my mouth shut.
I knew
you would never appear standing before me.
I had lost you 25 years before.
Since then,
I had grown from a fatherless child
into a middle-aged man.

zh: 雨声继续着，长夜在滴滴声中进行。我的心感到无比的寂寞。怎么，是屋漏么？我的脸颊湿了。
en:
The rain continued to fall.
The long night wore on amidst its dripping sound.
I was seized with acute loneliness.
Well, was the roof leaking?
Or was it my tears that had wetted my cheeks?

zh: 小时候我有一个愿望：我愿在你的庇荫下做一世的孩子。现在只有让梦来满足这个愿望了。
en:
When I was young,
I wished I could remain a kid forever
under your wing.
Now I can fulfill this wish
only in my dreams.

zh:
至少在梦里，我可以见到你，
我高兴，我没有挂虑地微笑，我不假思索地随口讲话。
en:
There in a dream,
I can at least come face to face with you.
I can be happy,
I can smile naive smiles,
I can chatter away freely.

zh:
为了这个，
我应该感谢梦。
en:
For all this,
I should be thankful to my dreams.

zh: 据说“至人无梦”。幸而我只是一个平庸的人。
en:
It is said that
" a virtuous man seldom dream".
Fortunately,
I am but an ordinary man.

zh: 清晨往松林里去散步，我在林荫路畔发见了一束被遗弃了的蔷薇。
en:
Rambling through a pine forest
early in the morning,
I came across a bunch of forsaken roses
lying by the shady wayside.

zh:
蔷薇的花色还是鲜艳的，
一朵紫红，一朵嫩红，一朵是病黄的象牙色中带着几分血晕。
en:
They were still fresh in colour.
One was purplish-red,
another pink,
still another a sickly ivory-yellow
slightly tinged with blood-red.

zh: 我把蔷薇拾在手里了。
en: I picked them up in my hand.

zh: 青翠的叶上已经凝集着细密的露珠，这显然是昨夜被除人遗弃了的。
en:
The numerous fine dewdrops
on the fresh green leaves
clearly showed that
the roses had just been cast away
the previous night.

zh: 这是可怜的少女/受了薄幸的男子的/欺给？
en:
Were they pitiful maidens
deflowered by fickle men?

zh: 还是不幸的青年/受了轻狂的的妇人的/玩弄？
en:
Or were they unlucky young men
fooled by frivolous women?

zh: 昨晚上甜蜜的私语，今朝的冷清的露珠......
en:
Last night's whispers of love;
this morning's drops of cold dew...

zh: 我把蔷薇拿到家里来了，我想找个花瓶来供养它。
en:
I brought the roses home
and tried to find a flower vase
to keep them in.

zh: 花瓶我没有，我在一只墙角上/寻了一个/断了颈子的/盛酒的/土瓶。
en:
Flower vase I had none,
but I did find in a nook of my room
an empty earthen wine bottle
with its neck broken.

zh:
普薇哟，我虽然不能供养你以春酒，
但我要供养你以清洁的流泉，(+和）清洁的素心。
en:
--O dear roses,
though unable to treat you to spring wine.
I could offer you limpid spring water
and my sincere pure heart.

zh: 你在这破土瓶中虽然不免要凄凄寂寂地飘零，但比遗弃/在路旁被人践踏了的好罢？
en:
Wouldn't it be better for you
to wither away in solitude
in this broken earthen wine bottle than to lie abandoned by the roadside and be trodden down upon?

zh: 我携着三个孩子在屋后草场中嬉戏着的时候，
en:
While my three kids,
accompanied by myself,
were frolicking about
on the meadow behind my house,

zh: 夕阳正烧着海上的天壁，眉痕的新月已经出现在鲜红的云缝里了。
en:
the sky above the distant edge of the sea
was aglow with the setting sun
and the crescent new moon
was already peeping out
from behind the scarlet clouds.

zh:
草场中放牧着的几条黄牛，,
好像在叫它们的主人快来牵它们回去。
en:
A few cows grazing on the pasture
let out a long drawn-out moo now and then
as if urging their master to lead them home
as quickly as possible.

zh: 我们的两匹母鸡和几只鸡雏，先先后后地从邻寺的墓地里跑回来了。
en:
Our two mother hens and their baby chicks
were scurrying homeward
one after another
from the grave yard of the nearby monastery.

zh: 母鸡们咯咯咯地叫了起来了，鸡雏们也调调地争食起来了。
en:
At the clucking of the hens,
the chicks serambled for the feed, chirping.

zh: “今年的成绩真好呢，竟养大了十只。”
en:
We've done quite well this year,
with ten chicks growing fast,
beamed my wife.

zh: 欢愉的音波，在金色的暮蕴中游泳。
en:
The joyous sound wave
drifted through the golden evening mist.

zh: 许久储蓄在心里的诗料，今晨在理发店里又浮上了心来了。
en:
My long pent-up poetic emotion
emerged again this morning
at a hairdresser's.

zh: 你年青的，年青的，远隔河山的姑娘哟，你的名姓我不曾知道，你恕我只能这样叫你了。
en:
O young lady,
you young lady of the distant land!
Excuse me for addressing you as "young lady",
for your name is still unknown to me.

zh:
那回是春天的晚上吧？
你替我剪了发，替我刮了面，替我盥洗了，又替我涂了香膏。
en:
It was probably on a spring evening.
You cut my hair, shaved my face,
gave me a shampoo
and applied some vanishing cream.

zh: 你最后替我分头的时候，我在镜中看见你替我拔去了一根白发。
en:
Finally,
in the mirror I saw you plucking out
a white hair from my head
while parting my hair.

zh: 啊，你年青的，年青的远隔河山的姑娘哟，
en: O young lady, you young lady of the distant land,【同上】

zh: 漂泊者自从那回离开你后又漂泊了三年，但是你的慧心替我把青春留住了。
en:
I have been leading a wandering life
for another three years
since I saw you last,
but it is your feeling heart
that has been the cause of my sustained youth.

zh: 水墨画
en: An Inkwash Painting

zh: 天空一片灰暗，没有丝毫的日光。
en:
The sky was a sheet of murky grey,
completely devoid of sunlight.

zh:
海水的蓝色浓得惊人，
乱岸的微波吐出群鱼噪喻的声韵。
en:
The sea was a ghastly dark blue.
The gentle waves
licking at the shore gave forth
a humming sound
like that of fish in shoals.

zh: 这是暴风雨欲来时的先兆。
en: All that foreboded a storm.

zh: 海中的岛屿和乌木的雕刻一样/静凝着了。
en:
Some isles in the sea
stood quiet and still
like ebony sculptures.

zh: 我/携着中食的饭匣/向沙岸上走来，在一只泊系着的渔舟里面坐着。
en:
I walked towards the sandy beach
carrying my lunch-box
and then sat inside a fishing boat
moored at the seashore.

zh: 一种淡白而无味的凄凉的情趣我把饭匣打开，又闭上了。
en:
What an insipid and dreary scene!
I opened the lunch-box
only to have it covered up again.

zh:
回头望见松原里的一座孤寂的火葬场。
红砖砌成的高耸的烟肉口上，冒出了一笔灰白色的飘忽的轻烟...
en:
Looking back,
I caught sight of a lonely crematorium
looming out of a pine wood.
Its towering red-brick chimney
was giving off wisps of grayish smoke.

zh: 昨朝我一个人在松林里徘徊，在一株老松树下戏筑了一座砂丘。
en:
Yesterday morning,
while wandering about alone in a pine forest,
I amused myself by piling up
a small sand-hill under an old pine tree.

zh: 我说，这便是我自己的坟墓了。
en: Let this be my own grave,said I.

zh: 我便拣了一块白石来写上了我自己的名字，把来做了墓碑。
en:
Picking up a piece of white stone,
I scribbled my name on it and said,
"Let this be my own gravestone."

zh: 我在墓的两旁/还移种了两株稚松/把它伴守。
en:
On either side of the grave,
I transplanted a pine sapling
to keep it company.

zh: 我今朝回想起来，又一人走来凭吊。
en:
This morning, recalling the grave,
I went to pay a visit to it.

zh: 但我已经走遍了这莽莽的松原，我的坟墓究竟往那儿去了呢？
en:
But the grave was nowhere to be found
though I searched
every nook and corner of the dense forest.
Where was it gone to?

zh:
啊，死了的我昨日的尸骸哟，哭墓的是你自己的灵魂，
我的坟墓究竟往那儿去了呢？
en:
O ye remains of my yesterday's dead self,
it was your own soul
that had come to mourn at the grave!
Where was my grave gone to?

zh: 有时走到艰难险阻的境界。（主语要译出）
en:
It is sometimes beset with
difficulties and obstacles

zh: 这是全靠雄健的精神才能冲过去的。
en:
and nothing short of a heroic spirit
can help surmount them.

zh: 一条浩浩荡荡的长江大河，有时流到很宽阔的境界，平原无际，一泻万里。
en:
A mighty long river
sometimes flows through
a broad section with
plains lying boundless on either side,
its waters rolling on non-stop
for thousands upon thousands of miles.

zh: 有时流到很逼狭的境界，两岸丛山迭岭，绝壁断崖，江河流于期间，回环曲折，极其险峻。民族生命的进展，其经历亦复如是。
en:
Sometimes it comes up against
a narrow section
flanked by high mountains and steep cliffs,
winding through a course with
many a perilous twist and turn.
A nation, in the course of its development,
fares likewise.

zh:
人类在历史上的生活正如（just like)旅行一样。
旅途上的征人所经过的地方，(“地方”范畴词不译）有时（now)是坦荡平原，有时（now)是崎岖险路。
en:
The historical course of man's life
is just like a journey.
A traveler on a long journey
passes through
now a broad, level plain,
now a rugged, hazardous road.

zh: (省略了“一个”）志于旅途的人，走到平坦的地方，因是高高兴兴地向前走，走到崎岖的境界，俞是奇趣横生，觉得在此奇绝壮绝的境界，俞能感到一种冒险的美趣。
en:
While a determined traveler
cheerfully continues his journey
upon reaching a safe and smooth place,
he finds it still more fascinating to
come to a rugged place,
the enormously magnificent spectacle of which,
he feels, is better able to
generate in him
a wonderful sensation of adventure.

zh: 中华民族现在所逢的史路，是一段崎岖险阻的道路。
en:
The Chinese nation is now confronted with
a rugged and dangerous section
of its historical course.

zh: (有转折意味）在这段道路上，实在亦有一种奇绝壮绝的境至，/使我们经过此段道路的人，感得一种壮美的趣味，
en:
Nevertheless,
there is also in this section
a spectacle of enormous magnificence that
inspires in us passers-by
a delightful sensation of splendor.

zh: (有转折意味）是非有雄健的精神的，不能够感觉到的。
en:
And this delightful sensation,
however,
can only be shared
by those with a heroic spirit.

zh: 我们的扬子江、黄河，(都）可以代表我们的民族精神，(为什么可以，因为）扬子江及黄河遇见沙漠、遇见山峡都是浩浩荡荡的往前流过去，以成其浊流滚滚，一泻万里的魄势（=气魄+态势=力量）。
en:
The Yangtse River and the Yellow River are both symbolic of our national spirit.
The two mighty rivers negotiate
deserts and gorges
until their turbid torrents
surge forward with irresistible force.

zh:
目前的艰难境界，那能（就是“不能”）阻抑我们民族生命的前进。我们应该拿出雄健的精神，高唱着进行的曲调，
在这悲壮歌声中，走过这崎岖险阻的道路。
要知在艰难的国运中建造国家，亦是人生最有趣味的事......
en:
The present national crisis
can never obstruct
the advance of our national life.
Let us brace up our spirits and
march through this rugged, dangerous road
to the tune of our solemn, stirring songs.
The greatest joy of life, mind you,
is to build up our country
during its most difficult days.

zh: 历史的道路，不会是坦平的，
en: The course of history is never smooth.

zh: 燕子去了，有再来的时候；杨柳枯了，在再青的时候；桃花谢了，有再开的时候。
en:
If swallows go away,
they will come back again.
If willows wither,
they will turn green again.
If peach shed their blossoms,
they will flower again.

zh: 但是，聪明的，你告诉我，我们的日子为什么一去不复返呢？
en:
But, tell me, you the wise,
why should our days go by
never to return?

zh: ——是有人偷了他们罢：那是谁？又藏在何处呢？是他们自己逃走了罢：现在又到了那里呢？
en:
Perhaps they have been stolen by someone.
But who could it be
and where could he hide them?
Perhaps they have just run away by themselves.
But where could they be
at the present moment?

zh: 我不知道他们给了我多少日子；但我的手确乎是渐渐空虚了。在默默里算着，八千多日子已经从我手中溜去；
en:
I don't know how many days
I am entitled to altogether,
but my quota of them
is undoubtedly wearing away.
Counting up silently,
I find that more than 8000 days
have already slipped away through my fingers.

zh: 像针尖上一滴水滴在大海里，我的日子滴在时间的流里，没有声音，也没有影子。我不禁头渗泼而泪潜潜了。
en:
Like a drop of water
falling off a needle point into the ocean,
my days are quietly dripping into
the stream of time without leaving a trace.
At the thought of this,
sweat oozes from my forehead
and tears trickle down my cheek.

zh: 去的尽管去了，来的尽管来着；去来的中间，又怎样地匆匆呢？
en:
What is gone is gone,
what is to come keeps coming.
How swift is the transition in between!

zh: 早上我起来的时候，小屋里射进两三方斜斜的太阳。
en:
When I get up in the morning,
the slanting sun casts
two or three squarish patches of light
into my small room.

zh: 太阳他也有脚啊，轻轻悄悄地挪移了；我也茫茫然跟着旋转。
en:
The sun has feet too,
edging away softly and stealthily.
And, without knowing it,
I am already caught in its revolution.

zh: 于是——洗手的时候，日子从水盆里过去；
吃饭的时候，日子从饭碗里过去；默默时，便从凝然的双眼前过去。
en:
vanishes in the rice bowl
when I have my meal;
passes away quietly
before the fixed gaze of my eyes
when I am lost in reverie.

zh: 我觉察他去的匆匆了，伸出手遮挽时，他又从遮挽着的手边过去，天黑时，我躺在床上，他便伶伶俐俐在从我身上跨过，从我脚边飞去了。
en:
Aware of its fleeting presence,
I reach out for it only to find it
brushing past my outstretched hands.
In the evening,
when I lie on my bed,
it nimbly strides over my body
and flits past my feet.

zh: 等我睁开眼和太阳再见，这算又溜走了一日。
en:
By the time
when I open my eyes to meet the sun again,
another day is already gone.

zh: 我掩着面叹息。但是新来的日子的影儿又开始在叹息里闪过了。
en:
I heave a 'sigh,
my head buried in my hands.
But, in the midst of my sighs,
a new day is flashing past.

zh: 在逃去如飞的日子里，在千门万户的世界里的我能做些什么呢？只有徘徊罢了，只有匆匆罢了；
en:
Living in this world
with its fleeting days and teeming millions,
what can I do
but waver and wander
and live a transient life?

zh: 在八千多日的匆匆里，除徘徊外，又剩些什么呢？
en:
What have I been doing
during the 8000 fleeting days
except wavering and wandering?

zh: 过去的日子如轻烟，被微风吹散了，如薄雾，被初阳蒸融了；
en:
The bygone days, like wisps of smoke,
have been dispersed by gentle winds,
and, like thin mists,
have been evaporated by the rising sun.

zh: 我留着些什么痕迹呢？我何曾留着像游丝样的痕迹呢？
en:
What traces have I left behind?
No, nothing,
not even gossamer-like traces.

zh: 我赤裸裸来到这世界，转眼间也将赤裸裸的回去罢？但不能平的，为什么偏要白白走这一遭啊？
en:
I have come to this world stark naked,
and in the twinkling of an eye,
I am to go back as stark naked as ever.
However, I am taking it very much to heart
why should I be made to
pass through this world for nothing at all?

zh: 你聪明的，告诉我，我们的日子为什么一去不复返呢？
en:
O you the wise,
would you tell me please:
why should our days
go by never to return?

zh:
我爱花，所以也爱养花。
我可还没成为养花专家，因为没有工夫去作研究与试验。
en:
I love flowers
and hence have taken to growing them.
But, short of time to
do research and experiment in flower cultivation,
I am no gardener at all.

zh: 我只把养花当作生活中的一种乐趣，花开的大小好坏都不计较，只要开花我就高兴。
en:
I merely take flower cultivation
as a pleasure of life.
I really don't care
whether or not my flowers
will put forth plump and nice-looking blossom.
I'll be delighted
as long as they can blossom.

zh: 在我的小院中，到夏天，满是花草，小猫儿们只好上房去玩耍，地上没有它们的运动场。
en:
In summer,
flowers and plants growing in luxuriance
in my small courtyard
will leave little open space
as a playground for the little cats,
so they have to sport about in our rooms instead.

zh: 花虽多，但无奇花异草。
en:
I grow many flowers,
but none of them are exotic or rare ones.

zh: 珍贵的花草/不易养活，看着一棵好花/生病欲死/是件难过的事。我不愿时时落泪。
en:
It is difficult to
grow a precious flower species.
And I feel bad to see
a good flower dying of illness.
I don't want often to shed tears over that.

zh: 北京的气候，对养花来说，不算很好。
en:
But Beijing's climate
is more or less unfit for
the growing of flowers.

zh: 冬天冷，春天多风，夏天不是干旱就是大雨倾盆；秋天最好，可是忽然会闹霜冻。
en:
Freezing in winter,
windy in spring,
and either too dry
or too often visited by rainstorms in summer.
While autumn is the best of all,
it is often plagued by a sudden frost.

zh: 在这种气候里，想把南方的好花养活，我还没有那么大的本事。
en:
In a climate like this,
it is far beyond my capacity
to grow precious flowers of southern breed.

zh: 因此，我只养些好种易活、自己会奋斗的花草。
en:
Therefore,
I only grow flowers and plants
that are hardy
and enjoy a high survival rate.

zh: 不过，尽管花草自己会奋斗，我若置之不理，任其自生自灭，(1+1=2)它们多数还是会死了的。
en:
Although such flowers are able to
weather through by themselves,
I, however never ignore them V1
or abandon them to their own fate, V2
for otherwise most of them
will probably end up dead.

zh: 我得天天照管它们，像好朋友似的关切他们。一来二去，我摸着一些门道：
en:
I have to care for them every day
as if they were my close friends.
Thus, in the course of time,
I've somehow
got the hang of flower cultivation

zh: 有的喜阴，就别放在太阳地里，有的喜干，就别多浇水。
en:
some flowers which are accustomed to
growing in the shade
should not be too much exposed to the sun.
Those which prefer dryness
should not be watered too often.
It gives me much pleasure to know
the right way of handling them.

zh: 这是个乐趣，摸住门道，花草养活了，而且三年五载老活着、开花，多么有意思呀！
en:
How interesting it is
to be able to keep my flowers and plants alive
and watch them thrive and bloom year in year out!

zh: 不是乱吹，这就是知识呀！多得些知识，一定不是坏事。
en:
It is no exaggeration to say that
there is much knowledge involved in this!
And the more knowledge one acquires,
the better it is of course.

zh: 我不是有腿病吗，不但不利于行，也不利于久坐。
en:
As I have some trouble with my leg,
I can't move around easily, V1
nor can I sit too long. V2

zh: 我不知道花草们受我的照顾，感谢我不感谢；我可得感谢它们。
en:
I don't know
if the flowers under my care
are grateful to me or not.
However, I wish for my part
to acknowledge my thanks to them.

zh: 在我工作的时候，我总是写了几十个字，就到院中去看看，浇浇这棵，搬搬那盆，
en:
I often leave off sedentary work
after writing a few dozen words
and go to the courtyard
to take a look at the flowers,
watering them and moving about the potted ones.

zh:
然后回到屋中再写一点，然后再出去，如此循环，
(结果）把脑力劳动与体力劳动结合到一起，有益身心，胜于吃药。
en:
Then I'll return to my room to write a bit more.
I'll go through the same back-and-forth process
again and again,
thus combining mental with manual labour.
This is a better way to
keep me fit in mind and body
than taking medicine.

zh: 要是赶上狂风暴雨或天气突变哪，就得全家动员，抢救花草，十分紧张。
en:
In case of/ a violent storm
or a sudden change of weather,
however, the whole family will have to
turn out to salvage the flowers and plants.
Everybody will then feel keyed up.

zh: 几百盆花，都要很快地抢到屋里去，使人腰酸腿疼，热汗直流。
en:
By the time
when we have managed to move
the several hundred potted flowers
to the rooms in a hurry,
we will be dog-tired
and wet with perspiration.

zh: 第二天，天气好转，又得把花儿都搬出去，就又一次腰酸腿疼，热汗直流。
en:
The next day, when the weather is fine,
we will have another round of being
dog-tired and wet with perspiration
in taking all the flowers out to the courtyard again.

zh: 可是，这多么有意思！不劳动，连棵花儿也养不活，这难道不是真理么？
en:
How interesting it is!
Isn't it true that
without doing manual labour,
we couldn't even keep a single flower alive?

zh: 送牛奶的同志，进门就夸“好香”！这使我们全家都感到骄傲。
en:
It filled the whole family with pride
whenever the milkman
exclaims on entering our gate,
" What a sweet smell!"

zh: 赶到县花开放的时候，约几位朋友来看看，更有秉烛夜游的神气—县花总在夜里放蕊。
en:
When the night-blooming cereuses
are about to be in flower,
we will invite some friends to visit us in the evening
to feast their eyes on them
-in an atmosphere smacking of
nocturnal merry-making under candle lights.

zh: 花儿分根了，一棵分为数棵，就赠给朋友们一些；
en:
When the cereuses have branched out,
we will pick some of the flowers
and give them as a present to our friends.

zh: 看着友人拿走自己的劳动果实，心里自然特别喜欢。
en:
We are of course especially happy to
see them take away our fruits of labour.

zh: 当然，也有伤心的时候，今年夏天这有这么一回。三百株菊秧还在地上，下了暴雨。
en:
Of course, there is a time to feel sad too.
Last summer, a rainstorm hit us
when 300 chrysanthemum
seedlings in the courtyard
were about to be transplanted to pots.

zh: 邻家的墙倒了下来，(+并且）菊秧被砸死者约三十多种，一百多棵！全家都几天没有笑容！
en:
Suddenly, the wall of our neighbour collapsed
and crushed more than 100 seedlings of 30 varieties.
The whole family were sad-faced
for quite a few days!

zh: 有喜有忧，有笑有泪，有花有实，有香有色，既须劳动，又长见识，这就是养花的乐趣。
en:
Joy and sorrow, laughter and tears,
flowers and fruit, fragrance and colour,
manual labour and increased knowledge
——all these make up
the joy of flower cultivation.

zh: 有这样一个故事。
en: There is a story which goes like this:

zh: 有人问：世界上什么东西的气力最大？
en:
Someone asked,
"What has the greatest strength on earth?"

zh: 回答纷绘的很，
en: The answers varied.

zh: 有的说“象”，有的说“狮”，
en:
Some said," The elephant."
Some said," The lion."

zh: 有人开玩笑似的说：是“金刚”，金刚有多少气力，当然大家全不知道。
en:
Some said jokingly,
"The fierce-browed guardian gods to Buddha."
But nobody of course could tell
how strong the guardian gods
were supposed to be.

zh: 结果，这一切答案完全不对，世界上气力最大的，是植物的种子。
en:
All the answers turned out
to be wide of the mark.
The mightiest thing on earth
is the seed of a plant.

zh: 一粒种子所可以显现出来的力，简直是超越一切，这儿又是一个故事。
en:
The great strength
which a seed is capable of
is simply matchless.
Here goes another story:

zh: 人的头盖骨，结合得非常致密与坚固，生理学家和解剖学者用尽了一切的方法，要把它完整在分出来，都没有这种力气，
en:
The bones forming a human skull
are so tightly and perfectly fit together
that all physiologists or anatomists,
hard as they try.
are powerless to take them apart
without damaging them.

zh: 后来忽然有人发明了一个方法，就是把植物的种子放在要解剖的头盖骨里，给它以温度与湿度，使它发芽，
en:
It so happened that,
at the suggestion of someone,
some seeds of plant
were placed inside
a human skull awaiting dissection
before heat and moisture
were applied to cause them to grow.

zh:
一发芽，这些种子便以可怕的力量，
将一切机械力所不能分开的骨骼，完整地分开了。
en:
Once they started to grow,
they let loose a terrific force
to separate all the skull bones,
leaving each of them intact.
This would have been impossible
with any mechanical power under the sun.

zh: 植物种子力量之大，如此如此。
en: See, how powerful the seeds of a plant can be!

zh: 这，也许特殊了一点，常人不容易理解，
en:
This story may be somewhat
too unusual for you to understand.

zh: 那么，你看见笋的成长吗？
en:
Well, have you ever seen
the growth of a bamboo shoot?

zh: 你看见被压在瓦砾和石块下面的一颗小草的生成吗？
en:
Or the growth of tender grass
from under a heap of rubble or rocks?

zh:
它为着向往阳光，为着达成它的生之意志，
不管上面的石块如何重，石块与石块之间如何狭，它必定要曲曲折折地，但是顽强不屈地透到地面上来，
en:
Seeking sunlight and survival,
the young plant will labour tenaciously
through twists and turns
to bring itself to the surface of the ground
no matter how heavy the rocks overhead may be
or how narrow the opening between them.

zh: 它的根往土壤里钻，它的芽往地面挺，
en:
While striking its roots deep into the soil,
the young plant pushes
its new shoots above-ground.

zh: 这是一种不可抗拒的力，阻止它的石块，结果也被它掀翻，
en:
The irresistible strength it can muster is
such as to overturn any rock in its way.

zh: 一粒种子的力量的大，如此如此。
en: See, how powerful a seed can be!

zh: 没有一个人将小草叫做“大力士”，但是它的力量之大，的确是世界无比，
en:
Though nobody describes
the little grass as a"husky",
yet its herculean strength
is unrivalled.

zh: 这种力，是一般人看不见的生命力，
en: It is the force of life invisible to the naked eye.

zh: 上面的石块，丝毫不足以阻挡，因为它是一种“长期抗战”的力，有弹性，能屈能伸的力，有韧性，不达目的不止的力。
en:
The rock is utterly helpless before this force
——a force that will forever remain militant,
a force that is resilient
and can take temporary set backs calmly,
a force that is tenacity itself
and will never give up until the goal is reached.

zh: 种子不落在肥土而落在瓦砾中，有生命力的种子决不会悲观和叹气，因为有阻力才有磨炼。
en:
When a seed falls under debris
instead of on fertile soil,
it never sighs in despair
because to meet with obstruction
means to temper itself.

zh: 生命开始的一瞬间就带了斗争来的草，才是坚韧的草，也只有这种草，才可以傲然地对那些玻璃棚中养育着的盆花哄笑。
en:
Indomitable is the grass
that begins its very life with a tough struggle.
It is only fit and proper
that the proud grass should be
jeering at the potted flowers in a glass house.

zh: 前些日子，林语堂先生似乎曾说过女子的唯一事业，是在结婚，
en:
The other day,
Mr. Lin Yutang said something to the effect that women's only career lies in matrimony.

zh: 现在一位法国大文豪来沪，对去访问他的新闻记者的谈话之中，又似乎说，男子欲成事业，应该不要结婚。
en:
Now, an eminent French writer
declared at a press interview
after arriving in Shanghai
that men should stay bachelors
if they want to achieve success in life.

zh:
华盛顿.欧文是一个独身的男子，
但《见闻短记》里的一篇歌颂妻子的文章，却写的那么优美可爱。
en:
Washington Irving was a confirmed bachelor,
but in his Sketch Book
there is an article extolling the wife as
a graceful and lovely life-long partner.

zh: 同样查而斯·兰姆也是独身的男子，而爱丽亚的《独身者的不平》一篇，
en:
Charles Lamb, also a single man,
in A Bachelor's Complaint of
the Behaviour of Married People,
one of his essays signed "Elia",

zh: 又冷嘲热讽，将结婚的男女和婚后必然的果子一小孩们一等，俏皮到了那一步田地。
en:
speaks mockingly of married people
with their inevitable postnuptial fruits
——the children.

zh: 究竟是结婚的好呢，还是不结婚的好？
en:
Marriage or no marriage,
which is more desirable?

zh: 这问题似乎同先有鸡还是先有鸡蛋一样，常常有人提起，而也常常没有人解决过的问题。
en:
That sounds like
the chicken-and-egg question,
which, though often discussed,
remains a perpetual puzzle.

zh: 照大体看来（=总的来说）,想租房子的时候，是无眷莫问的，
en:
Generally speaking,
one who has no family dependants
is not supposed to rent a house.

zh: 想做官的时候，又是朝里无裙莫做官的，想写文章的时候，是独身者不能写我的妻的，凡此种种似乎都是结婚的好。
en:
one who has no petticoat influence in the government
should refrain from becoming an official,
an unmarried male writer
is in no position to writer about "my wife".
All these seem to hint at the advantage of marriage.

zh: 可是要想结婚，第一要有钱，第二要有闲，第三要有职，这潘驴……的五个条件，却也不容易办到。
en:
But, to get married,
you need to have five perquisites,
namely, money, leisure, employment,
good looks and potentness,
of which all are not always available.

zh: 更何况结婚之后，“儿子自己要来”，
en:
What is more,
after your marriage,
your offspring
will come to this world of themselves.

zh: 在这世界人口过剩，经济恐慌，教育破产，世风不古的时候，
en:
And in a world with overpopulation,
economic crisis, educational bankruptcy
and deteriorating public morals,

zh: 万一不慎，同兰姆所说的一样，儿子们去上了断头台，
en:
they may, just as Charles Lamb says,
through their own acts of indiscretion,
be sent to the gallows.

zh: 那真是连祖宗三代的帽都要倒尽，那里还有什么“官人请！娘子请！”的唱随之乐可说呢？
en:
With such a terrible misfortune
befalling your family,
how could you still have
wedded bliss to speak of?

zh: 左思右想，总觉得结婚也不好的，不结婚也是不好的。
en:
Thinking the matter over and over again,
I cannot but come to the conclusion that
neither matrimony nor bachelorship
has anything to recommend itself.

zh: 前后加起来，我在北京已经住了四十多年，算是一个老北京了。
en:
I've been in Beijing
altogether for over 40years.
So I can well call myself
a long-timer of Beijing.

zh: 北京的名胜古迹，北京的妙处，我应该说是了解的；其他老北京当然也了解。
en:
Like all other long-timers of the city,
I'm supposed to be very familiar
with its scenic spots and historical sites,
nay, its superb attractions.

zh: 但是有一点，我相信绝大多数老北京并不了解，这就是黎明时分以前的北京。
en:
But I believe there is one thing lying unknown
to most of the long-time residents
-the predawn hours of Beijing.

zh:
多少年来，我养成了一个习惯：
每天早晨四点在黎明以前起床工作。
en:
For many years,
I have been in the habit of
getting up before daybreak
to start work at four.

zh: 我不出去跑步或散步，而是一下床就干活儿。
en:
Instead of going out for a jog or walk,
I'll set about my work as soon as I'm out of bed.

zh: 因此我对黎明前的北京的了解，是在屋子里感觉到的。
en:
As a result,
it is from inside my study
that I've got the feel of predawn Beijing.

zh:
我从前在什么报上读过一篇文章，
讲黎明时分天安门广场上的清洁工人。
en:
Years ago, I hit upon
a newspaper article about
street cleaner in Tian'anmen Square
at daybreak.

zh: 那情景必然是非常动人的，可惜我从未能见到，只是心向往之而已。
en:
It must have been
a very moving scene,
but what a pity
I haven't seen it with my own eyes.
I can only picture it
in my mind longingly.

zh: 四十年前，我住在城里在明朝曾经是特务机关的东厂里面。
en:
Forty years ago,
I lived downtown in Dongchang,
a compound which had housed
the secret service of the Ming dynasty.

zh: 几座深深的大院子，在最里面三个院子里只住着我一个人。
en:
There were inside it
several deep spacious courtyard
one leading into another.
I was the sole dweller
of the three innermost courtyards.

zh: 朋友们都说这地方阴森可怕，晚上很少有人敢来找我，我则怡然自得。
en:
My friends,
calling this place too ghastly,
seldom dared to come to see me in the evening
whereas I myself found it quite agreeable.

zh: 每当夏夜，我起床以后，立刻就闻到院子里那些高大的马绥花树散发出来的阵阵幽香，这些香气破窗而入，
en:
In summer,
the moment I got out of bed
before daybreak,
I would smell
the delicate fragrance
of the giant silk trees.
coming from outside my window.

zh: 我于此时神清气爽，乐不可支，连手中那一枝笨拙的笔也仿佛生了花。
en:
Thereupon,
I would feel refreshed and joyful,
and the clumsy pen in my hand
would seem to have become
as agile as it could.

zh: 几年以后，我搬到西郊来住，照例四点起床，坐在窗前工作。
en:
Several years later
when I moved to the western suburbs,
I kept my habit of rising at four
to begin work at the window.

zh: 白天透过窗子能够看到北京展览馆那金光闪闪的高塔的尖顶，此时当然看不到了。
en:
The glittering spire a top the tower
of the daytime through my window,
would no longer be visible now
in the early morning haze.

zh: 但是，我知道，即使我看不见它，它仍然在那里挺然耸入天空，仿佛想带给人以希望，以上进的劲头。
en:
Nevertheless I knew that,
tough invisible, it remained there intact,
towering to the skies to inspire people
with hope and the urge for moving ahead.

zh: 我仍然是乐不可支，心也仿佛飞上了高空。
en:
At this, I would be
beside myself with joy
and feel as if my heart were also
flying high up into the skies.

zh: 过了十年，我又搬了家。
en:
Ten years after,
I moved again.

zh: 这新居既没有马缕花，也看不到金色的塔顶。
en:
In the new home of mine,
I had no silk trees,
nor could I get sight of
the glittering spire from afar.

zh: 但是门前却有一片清碧的荷塘。
en:
There was, however,
a lotus pond of limpid blue
in front of my door.

zh: 刚搬来的几年，池塘里还有荷花。
en:
In the first few years
after I moved there,
lotus flowers continued to blossom
on the surface of the pond.

zh:
夏天早晨四点已经算是黎明时分。
在薄暗中透过窗子可以看到接天莲叶，而荷花的香气也幽然袭来，我顾而乐之，大有超出马缕花和金色塔顶之上的意味了。
en:
In the summer time,
when day broke early at four,
a vast stretch of lotus leaves
looking skywards outside my window
came dimly into sight
while the quiet fragrance of the lotus flowers
assailed my nose.
All that delighted me
even more than the silk trees
and the glittering spire.

zh: 难道我欣赏黎明前的北京仅仅由于上述的原因吗？不是的。
en:
Is it exclusively due to
the above-mentioned
that I've developed a liking for
predawn Beijing? No.

zh: 三十几年以来，我成了一个“开会迷”。
en:
For 30 years,
I've been bogged down
in the mire of meetings.

zh: 说老实话，积三十年之经验，我真有点怕开会了。
en:
To tell you the truth,
with the experience accumulated
over the 30 years,
I'm now scared of meetings.

zh: 说一句过火的话，我简直是提心吊胆，心里不得安宁。
en:
To exaggerate it a bit,
that keeps me in constant suspense
and makes me fidgety.

zh: 即使不开会，这种喘喘不安的心情总摆脱不掉。
en:
Even when no meeting is to take place,
I feel restless all the same.

zh: 只有在黎明以前，根据我的经验，没有哪里会来找你开会的。
en:
However, my experience tells
that it is only during the predawn hours
that I can be truly havened
from any involvement in meetings.

zh: 因此，我起床往桌子旁边一坐，仿佛有什么近似条件反射的东西立刻就起了作用，我心里安安静静，一下子进入角色，拿起笔来，
en:
As soon as I sit at my desk before dawn,
something similar to the conditioned reflex
will begin to function within me:
Instantly I'll pick up my pen
to play my proper part
with perfect peace of mind.

zh: “文思”（如果也算是文思的话）如泉水喷涌，记忆力也像刚磨过的刀子，锐不可当。
en:
Then inspiration comes gushing to my mind
and my memory becomes as quick as
a newly-sharpened knife.

zh: 当时，我真乐不可支，如果给我机会的话，我简直想手舞足蹈了。
en:
I'll feel overjoyed,
almost to the point of
waving my arms and stamping my feet.

zh: 因此，我爱北京，特别爱黎明前的北京。
en:
In short, I love Beijing,
especially predawn Beijing.

zh: 也许是我的精、气、神都不足吧，不但自己写不出长的东西，我读一本刊物时，也总是先挑短的看，不论是小说、散文或是其他的文学形式，最后才看长的。
en:
Perhaps due to my failing energies,
not only have I
refrained from writing anything long,
but also, in reading a magazine,
for example,
I usually finish its shorter pieces of writing first,
be they fiction, prose
or any other forms of literature
before going on to the longer ones.

zh: 我总觉得，凡是为了非倾吐不可而写的作品，都是充满了真情实感的。
en:
I always believe that anything
written with an irresistible inner urge
to unbosom oneself
must be full of genuine feelings.

zh: 反之，只是为写作而写作，如上之为应付编辑朋友，一之为多拿稿费，这类文章大都是尽量地往长里写，结果是即便的一点点的感情，也被冲洗到水分太多、淡而无味的地步。
en:
On the contrary,
if one writes simply for
the sake of writing-say,
to humour one's editor friends,
or worse still,
to earn more remuneration,
one will most probably
make his writings unnecessarily long
until they become,
despite what little feeling they may contain,
inflated and wishy-washy.

zh: 当由一个人物，一桩事迹，一幅画面而发生的真情实感，向你袭来的时候，它就像一根扎到你心尖上的长针，一阵卷到你面前的怒潮，你只能用最真切、最简练的文字，才能描画出你心尖上的那一阵剧痛和你面前的那一霎惊惶！
en:
When true emotions aroused by a person,
an event or a scene come upon you
like a pin pricking your heart
or an angry tide surging threateningly before you,
all you can do is
use the most vivid and succinct language
to describe the severe pain in your heart
or the momentary feeling of panic
caused by the angry tide.

zh: 我们伟大的祖国，是有写短文的文学传统的。
en:
Our great motherland
is known for its literary tradition of short essays.

zh: 那部包括上下数千年的《古文观止》，“上起东周，下迄明末，共选辑（=选择编辑=共录入）文章220篇”有几篇是长的？
en:
Do you find anything unduely long
in A Treasury of Best Ancient Chinese Prose
with its 220 essays selected from
a period of several thousand years in ancient China
from the Eastern Zhou Dynasty
down until the end of the Ming Dynasty?

zh:
如杜牧的《阿房宫赋》，韩愈的《祭十二郎文》等等，哪一篇不是短而充满了真情实感？
今人的巴金的《随感录》，不也是一个实例吗？
en:
Aren't the essays in it,
like Du Mu's Rhapsody on Epang Palace
and Han Yu's
An Elegiac Address to My Nephew Shi'erlang,
all short and yet full of true feelings?
Isn't A Collection of Random Thoughts by Ba Jin,
our contemporary,
another like example of pithy writing?

zh: 读最近一期的《文学评论》，
en:
In the latest issue of
the Literary Review,

zh: 里面有几篇关于“红学”的文章，引起了我的注意。
en:
several articles on Redology
have attracted my attention.

zh:
有的作者既反省，又批判。
有的作者从困境中找出路。
有的作者慨叹，“红学”出了危机。

如此等等，煞是热闹。
文章的论点都非常精彩，很有启发。
en:
and so on and so forth.
The discussion is quite animated.
The arguments set forth in articles
are very interesting and enlightening.

zh: 但是，我却忽然想到了一个怪问题：这样的“红学”有用处吗？
en:
Nevertheless,
a strange question has occurred to me:
Is this kind of Redology
of any use at all?

zh: 对红学家本身，对在大学里和研究所里从事文学理论研究的人，当然有用。
en:
It is of course useful
to the Redologists themselves
as well as to those
engaged in the study of literary theory
at universities and research institutes.

zh: 但是对广大的《红楼梦》的读者呢？我看是没有用处。
en:
But, to my mind,
it is of little use
to readers of A Dream of Red Mansions
at large.

zh: 《红楼梦》问世二百年以来，通过汉文原文和各种译文读过本书的人，无虑多少个亿。
en:
Ever since
the publication of this novel
some 200 years ago,
hundreds of millions of people
have read its Chinese original
or its translations in various languages.

zh:
这样多的读者哪一个是先看批评家的文章，
然后再让批评家牵着鼻子走，按图索翼地去读原作呢？我看是绝无仅有。
en:
Of these innumerable people,
how many have read the novel
by starting with
a perusal of critics' articles
and allowing themselves
to be led by the nose by the critics
as to how to read the novel?
Next to none.

zh: 一切文学作品，特别是像《红楼梦》这样伟大的作品，内容异常地丰富，涉及到的社会层面异常地多，简直像是一个宝山，一座迷宫。
en:
All literary works,
especially a monumental one
like A Dream of Red Mansions,
are extremely rich in content
and involve diverse social strata
- to such an extent that
they virtually resemble
a mountain of treasure or a labyrinth.

zh: 而读者群就更为复杂，不同的家庭背景，不同的社会经历，不同的民族，不同的国家，不同的文化传统，不同的心理素质，不同的年龄，不同的性别，不同的职业，不同的爱好
en:
And the readers
are even more complicated,
differing from each other
in family background, social experience,
nationality, country, cultural tradition,
psychological condition, age, sex,
profession, hobby, etc., etc.

zh: 还可以这样“不同”下去，就此打住——，
en:
The list could go on endlessly,
so I wouldn't mind stopping here.

zh: 他们来读《红楼梦》，会各就自己的特点，欣赏《红楼梦》中的某一个方面，
en:
They will each appreciate
a certain aspect of the novel
according to their own individuality.

zh: 受到鼓舞，受到启发，引起了喜爱；也可能受到打击，引起了憎恶，总之是千差万别。
en:
They may feel
inspired and enlightened,
and hence love it,
or they may feel hurt,
and hence loathe it.
In short, the reactions vary.

zh: 对这此读者来说，“红学家”就好像是住在“太虚幻境”里的圣人、贤人，与自己无关。
en:
To. them,
the Redologists
seem to be sages and men of virtue
residing in
the "Illusory Land of Great Void"
and having nothing
whatsoever to do with them.

zh: 他们不管“红学家”究竟议论些什么，只是读下去，读下去。
en:
They, just read on and on,
caring not
what the Redologists may say.

zh: 因此我说，文学批评家无用。
en:
Therefore, I reiterate,
literary criticism is useless.

zh: 不但对读者无用，对作者也无用。
en:
It is useless
not only to the readers,
but also to writers.

zh: 查一查各国文学史，我敢说，没有哪一个伟大作家是根据文学批评家的理论来进行创作的。
en:
Looking up the literary history
of each and every country,
I dare say that
none of the world's great literary figures
ever did their writing
in line with the theory of literary critics.

zh: 那么，文学批评家的研究不就是毫无意义了吗？也不是的。
en:
On the other hand, however,
does it follow that
the research
done by literary critics
is totally meaningless?
No, that is not true either.

zh: 他们根据自己的文学欣赏的才能，根据不同时代潮流，
en:
In accordance with
their own capacity for
literary appreciation
and the different historical trends,

zh: 对文学作品提出自己的看法，互相争论，互相学习，互相启发，互相提高，这也是一种创作活动，对文学理论的建设会有很大的好处。
en:
the views they put forward for
mutual discussion, study,
inspiration and improvement
are also something creative
and conducive to
the development of literary theory.

zh: 只是不要幻想，自己的理论会对读者和作者有多大影响。
en:
Only they should be
under no illusion
about their theories
exerting powerful influence
on the readership or writers.

zh: 这样一来，就可以各安其业，天下太平了。
en:
That is the way for each
to have a role of his own to play
and for peace to reign under heaven.

zh: 上面这些话其实只有幼儿园的水平，
en:
What I've said above
is only skin-deep,
of kindergarten level.

zh: 可是还没有见有什么人这样坦率地说出来。
en:
But so far none else
have ventured to
be equally can did.

zh: 就让我当一个“始作俑者”吧！
en:
Therefore,
let me be reconciled
to being saddled with
the epithet of
" originator of a bad practice".

zh: 寒暑表（=温度计）降到冰点（=零度）下十八度的时候，我们也是在廊下睡觉。
en:
The thermometer had dropped to
18 degrees below zero,
but we still chose to
sleep in the porch as usual.

zh: (+对我而言）每夜最熟识的就是天上的星辰了。
en:
In the evening,
the most familiar sight to me
would be stars in the sky.

zh: 也不过只是点点闪烁的光明，而相看惯了，偶然不见，也有些想望与无聊。
en:
Though they were
a mere sprinkle of twinkling dots,
yet I had become so accustomed to them
that their occasional absence
would bring me loneliness and ennui.

zh: 连夜雨雪，一点星光都看不见。
en:
It had been snowing all night,
not a single star in sight.

zh: 荷（指一个人）和我拥袅对坐，在廊子的两角，遥遥谈话。
en:
My roommate and I,
each wrapped in a quilt,
were seated far apart in
a different corner of the porch,
facing each other and chatting away.

zh: 荷指着说：“你看维纳斯（Venus)升起来了！”
en:
She exclaimed
pointing to something afar,
" Look, Venus is rising!"

zh: 我抬头望时，却是山路转折处的路灯。
en:
I looked up
and saw nothing but a lamp
round the bend
in a mountain path.

zh: 我怡然一笑，也指着对山的一星灯火说：“那边是丘比特（Jupiter)呢！”
en:
I beamed and said pointing to
a tiny lamplight
on the opposite mountain,
"It's Jupiter over there!"

zh: 愈指愈多。
en:
More and more lights
came into sight
as we kept pointing here and there.

zh: 松林中射来零乱的风灯，都成了满天星宿。
en:
Lights from hurricane lamps
flickering about
in the pine forest
created the scene of
a star-studded sky.

zh: 真的，雪花隙里，看不出天空和森林的界限，将繁灯当作繁星，简直是抵得过。
en:
With the distinction
between sky and forest
obscured by snowflakes,
the numerous lamp-lights
now easily passed for as many stars.

zh: 一念至诚的将假作真，灯光似乎都从地上飘起。
en:
Completely lost in make-believe world,
I seemed to see all the lamp-lights
drifting from the ground.

zh: 这幻成的星光，都不移动，不必半夜梦醒时，再去追寻它们的位置。
en:
With the illusory stars
hanging still overhead,
I was spared the effort of tracing their positions
when I woke up from my dreams
in the dead of night.

zh: 于是雨雪寂寞之夜，也有了慰安了。
en:
Thus I found consolation
even on a lonely snowy night.

zh: 最令人忧目惊心的一件事，是看着钟表上的秒针一下一下的移动，每移动一下就是表示我们的寿命已经缩短了一部分。
en:
It is most startling
to hear a watch or clock
clicking away the seconds,
each click indicating
the shortening of one's life by a little bit.

zh: 再看看墙上挂着的可以一张张撕下的日历，每天撕下一张就是表示我们寿命又缩短了一天，
en:
Likewise,
with each page torn off the wall calendar,
one's life is shortened by another day.

zh: 因为时间即生命，没有人不爱惜他的生命，但很少人珍视他的时间。
en:
Time, therefore, is life.
Nevertheless, few people
treasure their time as much as their life.

zh: 如果想在有生之年做一点什么事，学一点什么学问，充实自己，帮助别人，使生命成为有意义，不虚此生，那么就不可浪费光阴。
en:
Time must not be wasted
if you want to do your bit
in your remaining years
or acquire some useful knowledge
to improve yourself and help others,
so that your life may turn out to be
significant and fruitful.

zh: 这道理人人都懂，
en: All that is fool proof,

zh: 可是很少人真能积极不懈的善为利用他的时间。
en:
yet few people really strive to
make the best use of their time.

zh: 我自己就是浪费了很多时间的一个人。
en:
Personally,
I am also a fritterer.

zh: 我不打麻将，我不经常的听戏看电影，几年中难得一次，我不长时间看电视，通常只看半个小时，我也不串门子闲聊天。
en:
I don't play mahjong.
I seldom go to the theatre or cinema
-I go there maybe only once every few years.
I seldom spend long hours watching TV
—usually I watch TV
for no more than 30 minutes at a sitting.
Nor do I go visiting and gossiping from door to door.

zh: 有人问我：“那么你大部分时间都做了些什么呢？”
en:
Some people asked me,
"Then what do you do
with most of your time?"

zh: 我痛自反省，我发现，除了职务上的必须及人情上所不能免的活动外，我的时间大部分都浪费了。
en:
Introspecting with remorse,
I found that apart from the time
earmarked for my job
and unavoidable social activities.
most of my time had been wasted.

zh: 我应该集中精力，读我所未读过的书，我应该利用所有时间，写我所要写的东西。
en:
I should have concentrated
my energies on reading
whatever books I have not yet read.
I should have utilized all my time
in writing anything I want to write.

zh: 但是我没能这样做。我的好多时间都糊里糊涂的混过去了，“少壮不努力，老大徒伤悲。”
en:
But I've failed to do so.
Very much of my times has been
frittered away aimlessly.
As the saying goes,
"One who does not work hard in youth
will grieve in vain in old age."

zh: 例如我翻译莎士比亚，
en: Take the translation of Shakespeare for example.

zh: 本来计划于课余之暇每年翻译两部，二十年即可完成，
en:
I had initially planned to spend
20 years of my spare time
in doing the translation,
finishing two plays a year.

zh: 但是我用了三十年，主要的原因是懒。
en:
But I spent 30 years instead,
due primarily to
my slothfulness.

zh: 翻译之所以完成，主要的是因为活得相当长久，十分惊险。
en:
The whole project
would probably have fallen through
had it not been for my fairly long life.

zh: 翻译完成之后，虽然仍有工作计划，但体力渐衰，有力不从心之感。
en:
After that
I had other plans for work,
but, because of my approaching senility,
somehow I failed to do
what I had wished to.

zh: 假使（+在）年轻的时候鞭策自己，
en: Had I spurred myself on/ in my youth,

zh: 如今当有较好或较多的表现。
en:
I would have done
more and better work.

zh: 然而悔之晚矣。
en: Alas, it is too late to repent.

zh: 再例如，作为一个中国人，经书不可不读。
en:
Another example.
The reading of Chinese classics
is a must for all Chinese.

zh: (+但）我年三十才知道读书自修的重要。
en:
But it was not until
I was over 30
that I came to realize the importance of
self-study in the matter of classics.

zh: 我披阅，我圈点。
en:
I did read carefully though,
marking words and phrases
for special attention
with small circles and dots.

zh: 但是恒心不足，时作时辍。
en:
But my efforts at self-study
were off and on.

zh: 五十以学易，可以无大过矣，我如今年过八十，还没有接触过《易经》，说来惭愧。
en:
Confucius says,
"I shall be free of great faults
if I can live long enough
to begin the study of Yi at the age of 50."
I feel ashamed to admit that
I haven't even touched Yi
though I'm now over 80.

zh: 史书也很重要。
en:
Chinese history book
are equally important.

zh: 我出国留学的时候，
en:
father bought a set of
the Tong Wen lithographic edition of
the First Four Books of History.

zh: 塞满了我的行筷的一半空间，
en:
and crammed them
into my travelling box,
taking up half of its space.

zh: 我在外国混了几年之后又把前四史原封带回来了。
en:
Several years later, however,
after drifting along abroad,
I returned home carrying with me
the same books all unread.

zh: 直到四十年后才鼓起勇气读了《通鉴》一遍。
en:
It was not until 40 years later
that I plucked up enough courage
to read through Dong Jian.

zh: 现在我要读的书太多，深感时间有限。
en:
So many books still remain to be read,
and I much regret
not having enough time to do it.

zh: 无论做什么事，健康的身体是基本条件。
en:
Whatever you do,
you need a sound body first of all.

zh: 我在学校读书的时候，有所谓“强迫运动”，
en:
In my school days,
in response to
the so-called "compulsory physical exercises"

zh: 我踢破过几双球鞋，打断过几只球拍。因此侥幸维持下来最低限度的体力。
en:
I went in for many sports
at the expense of
many pairs of sneakers and rackets,
thus luckily building up
a minimum of good physique.

zh: 老来打过几年太极拳，且前则以散步活动筋骨而已。
en:
When I was approaching old age,
I did Tai ji quan (shadow boxing)
for several years.
Now I only do some walking exercises.

zh: 寄语年轻朋友，千万要持之以恒的从事运动，这不是嬉戏，不是浪费时间。
en:
Dear young friends,
my advice to you is:
Do physical exercises perseveringly.
That has nothing to do with
merry-making or time-wasting.

zh: 健康的身体是作人做事的真正的本钱。
en:
Good health is
the wherewithal for
a successful life and career.

zh: 不要抛弃学问 胡适
en: Never Give Up the Pursuit of Learning Hu Shih

zh: 诸位毕业同学，你们现在要离开母校了，我没有什么礼物送给你们，只好送你们一句话罢。（=别的礼物我没有，除了一句话）
en:
Dear students of the Graduating Class,
As you are leaving your alma mater,
I have nothing to offer you as a gift
except a word of advice.

zh: 这一句话是：“不要抛弃学问。”
en:
My advice is,
" Never give up the pursuit of learning."

zh: 以前的功课也许有一大部分是为这张文凭，不得已而做的，
en:
You have perhaps finished
your college courses mostly
for obtaining the diploma,
or, in other words,
out of sheer necessity.

zh: 从今而后，你们可以依自己的心愿去自由研究了。
en:
However, from now
you are free to follow your own bent
in the choice of studies.

zh: 趁现在年富力强的时候，努力做一种学问。
en:
While you are in the prime of life,
why not devote yourselves
to a special field of study?

zh: 少年是一去不复返的，等到（你）精力衰时，努力做学问也来不及了。
en:
Youth will soon be gone never to return.
And it will be too late for you
to go into scholarship
when in your declining years.

zh: 即为吃饭计，学问决不会辜负人的。
en:
Knowledge will do you a good turn
even as a means of subsistence.

zh: 吃饭而不求学问，三年五年后，你们都将要被后来少年淘汰掉的。
en:
If you give up studies while holding a job,
you will in a couple of years
have had yourselves replaced by
younger people.

zh: 到那时再想做点学问来补救，恐怕已太晚了。
en:
It will then be too late
to remedy the situation
by picking up studies again.

zh: 有人说：“出去做事之后，生活问题急需解决，哪有工夫去读书？即使要做学问，既没有图书馆，又没有实验室，哪能做学问？”
en:
Some people say,
"Once you have a job,
you'll come up against
the urgent problem of making a living.
How can you manage to find time to study?
Even if you want to, will it be possible with no library or no laboratory available?"

zh: 我要对你们说：
en: Now let me tell you this.

zh:
凡是要等到有了图书馆才读书的，有了图书馆也不肯读书。
凡是要等到有了实验室才做研究的，有了实验室也不肯做研究。
en:
Those who refuse to study
for lack of a library
will most probably continue to do so
even though there is a library.
And those who refuse to do research
for lack of a laboratory
will most probably continue to do so
even though a laboratory is available.

zh: 你有了决心要研究一个问题，自然会搏衣节食去买书，自然会想出来法子来设置仪器。
en:
As long as you set your mind on studies,
you will naturally cut down on food and clothing
to buy books or do everything possible
to acquire necessary instruments.

zh: 至于时间，更不成问题。达尔文一生多病，不能多作工，每天只能做一点钟的工作。
en:
Time is no object.
Charles Darwin could only
work one hour a day due to ill health.

zh: 你们看他的成绩！每天花一点钟看10页有用的书，每年可看3600多页书，30年可读11万页书。
en:
Yet what a remarkable man he was!
If you spend one hour a day
reading 10 pages of a book,
you can finish more than 3,600 pages a year,
and 110,000 pages in 30 years.

zh: 诸位，11万页书可以使你成一个学者了，
en:
Dear students,
110,000 pages will be quite enough
to make a learned man of you.

zh: 可是，每天看三种小报也得费你一点钟的工夫，四圈麻将也得费你一点半钟的光阴。看小报呢，还打麻将呢？还是努力做一个学者呢？全靠你们自己的选择！
en:
It will take you one hour
to read three tabloids a day,
and one and half hours
to finish four rounds of mah-jong a day.
Reading tabloids, playing mah-jong
or striving to be a learned man,
the choice lies with you.

zh: 易卜生说：“你的最大责任是把你这块材料铸造成器。”
en:
Henrik Ibsen says,
"it is your supreme duty
to cast yourself into a useful implement."

zh: 学问便是铸器的工具。抛弃了学问便是毁了你们自己。
en:
Learning is the casting mould.
Forsake learning,
and you will ruin yourself.

zh: 再会了！你们的母校眼睁睁地要看你们十年之后成什么器。
en:
Farewell!
Your alma mater is watching eagerly
to see what will become of you
ten years from now.

zh: 在电影刊物上看见一个影片的名字：《我若为王》。
en:
Recently in a movie magazine
I came across the title of a film:
If I Were King.

zh: 从这影片的名字，我想到和影片毫无关系的另外的事。
en:
It has put me in mine of
something entirely foreign
to film in question.

zh: 我想，自己如果作了王，这世界会成为一种怎样的光景呢？
en:
I wonder
what would become of this world
if I myself were king.

zh: 这自然是一种完全可笑的幻想，我根本不想作王，也根本看不起王，王是什么东西呢？
en:
This is of course a ridiculous fancy,
for being a king is the last thing I aspire to
and also a thing I utterly despise.
What the hell is a king?

zh: 难道我脑中还有如此封建的残物么？
en:
How can I still be
so feudalistic in my mind?

zh: 而且真想作王的人，他将用他的手去打天下，决不会放在口里说的。
en:
Moreover,
if one is really bent on being a king,
he will try to carry out his design
by deeds instead of by words.

zh: 但是假定又假定，我若为王，这个世界会成为一种怎样的光景？
en:
But, to put it hypothetically,
suppose I were king,
what would this world look like?

zh: 我若为王，自然我的妻就是王后了。
en:
If I were king,
my wife would of course be queen.

zh: 我的妻的德性，我不怀疑，为王后只会有余的。
en:
With all her moral excellence,
of which I make no doubt,
she would be more than qualified
for being a queen.

zh: 但纵然没有任何德性，纵然不过是个姐妓，那时候，她也仍旧是王后。
en:
But even if she had no virtue to speak of,
or were just a whore,
she would be queen all the same.

zh:
一个王后是如何地尊贵呀，
会如何地被人们像捧着天上的星星一样捧来捧去呀，假如我能够想像，那一定是一件有趣的事情。
en:
Imagine how noble and dignified
a queen would be
and how people would keep lauding her
to the skies like mad!
It is indeed great fun for me
to visualize all of this.

zh: 我若为王，我的儿子，假如我有儿子，就是太子或王子了。
en:
If I were king,
my son, if any,
would be crown prince or prince.

zh: 我并不以为我的儿子会是一无所知，一无所能的白痴，
en:
I don't think my son
will be ignorant or worthless
in every way like an idiot.

zh: 但纵然是一无所知一无所能的白痴，也仍旧是太子或王子。
en:
But, even if that were not the case,
he would still be crown prince or prince.

zh: 一个太子或王子中如何地尊贵呀，会如何被人们像捧天上的星星一样地捧来捧去呀。假如我能想像，倒是件不是没有趣味的事。
en:
Imagine how noble and dignified
a crown prince or prince would be
and how people would keep lauding him
to the skies like mad!
It is indeed great fun for me
to visualize all of this.

zh: 我若为王，我的女儿就是公主，我的亲眷都是皇亲国戚。
en:
If I were the king,
my daughters would be princess,
and my relatives by marriage
would all become
members of the royal family.

zh:
无论他们怎样丑陋，怎样顽劣，怎样......
也会被人们像捧天上的星星一样地捧来捧去，因为她们是贵人。
en:
No matter how ugly or perverse
or what not they were,
people would keep lauding them
to the skies like mad just the same
because they were dignitaries.

zh: 我若为王，我的姓名就会改作：“万岁”，我的每一句话都成为：“圣旨”。
en:
If I were king,
I would be addressed as "Your Majesty"
and every word of mine
would become a "royal edict".

zh: 我的意欲，我的贪念，乃至每一个幻想，都可竭尽全体臣民的力量去实现，即使是无法实现的。
en:
All my subjects
would leave no stone unturned
to carry out every will,
every avaricious desire
and even every whim of mine,
even though they were
all beyond the possible.

zh: 我将没有任何过失，因为没有人敢说它是过失；
en:
I would do no wrong simply,
because no one dared to
call it a wrong.

zh: 我将没有任何罪行，因为没有人敢说它是罪行。
en:
I would commit no crime simply
because no one dared to
call it a crime.

zh: 没有人敢呵斥我，指摘我，除非把我从王位上赶下来。但是赶下来，就是我不为王了。
en:
No one would dare to
berate or find fault with me
unless I was removed from the throne,
which meant that
I was no longer the king.

zh: 我将看见所有的人们在我面前低头，鞠躬，匍盒，连同我的尊长，我的师友，和从前曾在我面前昂头阔步耀武扬威的人们。
en:
I would see all people
hang their heads, bow low
or prostrate themselves at my feet,
including my respected elders, teachers, friends
and even those
who had used to swagger arrogantly
in front of me.

zh: 我将看不见一个人的脸，所看见的只是他们的头顶或帽盔。
en:
I could see none of their faces;
all I could see were
the tops of their heads
or hats or helmets on their heads.

zh: 或者所能看见的脸都是谄媚的，乞求的，
en:
The only faces I could see
would be ingratiating or supplicating

zh: 快乐的时候不敢笑，不快乐的时候不敢不笑，
悲戚的时候不敢哭，不悲戚的时候不敢不哭脸。
en:
faces that dared not cry
to express sorrow;
faced that dared not
refrain from a feigned cry
when there was no sorrow
to justify a cry.

zh: 我将听不见人们的真正的声音，
en: I could hear no true voices of my people.

zh: 所能听见的都是低微的，柔婉的，畏葸的和娇痴的，唱小旦的声音：
en:
All I could hear would be
the feeble, soft, timid and affected voice,
like that of a female Peking opera singer,
chanting,

zh: “万岁，万岁！万万岁！”这是他们的全部语言。
en:
Long live the King!
that would be their language in toto.

zh: “有道明君！伟大的主上啊！”这就是那语言的全部内容。
en:
Great is the King,
our enlightened lord!
That would be
the sole content of their language.

zh: 没有在我之上的人了，没有和我同等的人了，
en:
There would be no one above me
or on an equal footing with me.

zh: 我甚至会感到单调，寂寞和孤独。
en:
I would even feel
bored, lonely and isolated.

zh: 为什么人们要这样呢？为什么要捧我的妻，捧我的儿女和亲眷呢？
en:
Why would people behave like that?
Why would they flatter my wife,
my children and my relatives?

zh: 因为我是王，是他们的主子，
en: Because I was king, their master.

zh: 我将恍然大悟：我生活在这些奴才们中间，连我所敬畏的尊长和师友也无一不是奴才，而我自己不过是一个奴才的首领。
en:
It would suddenly dawn on me that
living among these flunkeys,
including my esteemed elders,
teachers and friends,
I myself,too,
was nothing but a mere head flunkey.

zh: 我是民国的国民，
en: I am the citizen of the Republic.

zh:
民国国民的思想和生活习惯
使我深深地憎恶一切奴才或奴才相，连同敬畏的尊长和师友们。
en:
Being accustomed to the mode of thinking
and living of a republican citizen,
I would deeply abhor all servility and flunkeys,
including my esteemed elders, teachers and friends.

zh: 请科学家们不要见笑，
en:
Dear scientists,
please don't laugh at me.

zh: 我以为世界之所以还有待于改进者，全因为有这些奴才的缘故。
en:
Methinks
the world is very much
in need of reform simply
because of
the presence of these flunkeys,

zh:
生活在奴才们中间，作奴才们的首领，
我将引为生平的最大耻辱，最大的悲哀。
en:
I would regard it as
the deepest disgrace and sorrow of my life
to live among the flunkeys
and become their chief.

zh:
我将变成一个暴君，或者反而是明君；
我将把我的臣民一齐杀死，连同尊长和师友，不准一奴种留在人间。
en:
I would rather become
a tyrant or an enlightened king
so that I could kill off all my subjects,
among them my respected elders,
teachers and friends,
and have the flunkey species
exterminated once for all.

zh: 我将没有一个臣民，我将不再是奴才们的君主。
en:
Then, with all my subjects gone,
I would no longer be
the king of flunkeys.

zh:
我若为王，将终于不能为王，
却也真地为古今中外最大的王了。
en:
If I were king
and ultimately ended up
becoming no king at all,
I would indeed be the greatest king
that had ever breathed since time immemorial.

zh: “万岁，万岁，万万岁！”我将和全世界的真的人们一同三呼。
en:
I would join true people all the world over in
giving three cheers for myself.

zh: 作家有三种死法。一曰自然的死，二曰痛苦的死，三曰快乐的死。
en:
A writer can die
three kinds of death:
natural death,
painful death, happy death.

zh: 自然的死属于心脏停止跳动，是一种普遍的死亡形式，没有特色，可以略而不议。
en:
Natural death,
caused by the discontinuation of heartbeat,
is a common form of death
with no characteristics of its own,
and therefore may as well
be left out without any comment.

zh: 快乐的死和痛苦的死不属于心脏停止跳动，是人还活着，作品已经、或几乎是没有了！
en:
In the case of
happy death and painful death,
which are not caused by
the discontinuation of heartbeat,
the writer,alive as he is,
has stopped or almost stopped writing!

zh: 作家没有了作品，可以看作是个人艺术生命的死亡、职业的停顿。
en:
When a writer
no longer produces any works,
it is tantamount to
the death of his artistic life
or the end of his career.

zh: 其中有些人是因为年事已高，力不从心。
en:
Some writers lay down their pens
because they are
too old to be equal to the task.

zh: 这不是艺术的死亡，而是艺术的离休，
en:
We call it retirement from art
rather than death of art.

zh: 他自己无可自责，社会也会尊重他在艺术上曾经作出的贡献。
en:
They have nothing to blame themselves for.
And society at large
will pay tribute to the contributions
they have already made to art.

zh: 痛苦的死亡却不然，即当一个作家的体力和脑力还能胜任创作的时候，作品已经没有了，其原因主要是由于各种苦难和折磨（包括自我折磨）所造成。
en:
Painful death is quiet another matter.
It occurs when a writer abandons writing
even though he is still sound in mind and body.
It results mainly from
various kinds of sufferings and torments
(including self-inflicted torments).

zh: 折磨毁了他的才华，苦难消沉了意志，作为人来说他还活着，作为作家来说却正在或已死去。
en:
Torments ruin his talent
while sufferings demoralize him.
Though still alive as a man,
he is dying or already dead as a writer.

zh: 这种死亡他自己感到很痛苦，别人看了心里也很难受。
en:
This kind of death
causes not only much pain
to the writer himself,
but much sadness
to other people as well.

zh: 快乐的死亡却很快乐，不仅他自己感到快乐，别人看来也很快乐。
en:
Happy death is a joyful thing,
bring happiness to
both the writer himself and other people.

zh:
昨天看见他大会上做报告，下面掌声如雷；
今天又看见他参加宴会，为这为那地频频举杯。
en:
Yesterday we saw him
addressing a big meeting
amidst thunderous applause,
and today we saw him attending a banquet,
drinking nonstop to this and that.

zh: 昨天听见他在高朋中大发议论，语惊四座，
en:
Yesterday we heard him
talking volubly to
a gathering of distinguished guests,
capturing the attention of all present,

zh: 今天又听见他在那些开不完的座谈会上重复昨天的意见。
en:
and today we heard him
repeating himself
at one of those endless forums.

zh: 昨天看见他在北京的街头，今天又看见他飞到了广州......
en:
Yesterday we met him
on a Beijing street,
and today we saw him
flying to Guangzhou...

zh: 只是看不到或很少看到他的作品发表哪里。
en:
But never or every seldom
do we find his new works
seeing the light of day.

zh: 我不害怕自然的死，因为害怕也没用，人人不可避免。
我也不太害怕痛苦的死，因为那时代已经过去。
en:
Nor do I fear painful death
for it is something belonging to
a bygone age.

zh: 我最害怕的就是那快乐的死，毫无痛苦，十分热闹，甚至还有点轰轰烈烈。
en:
What I fear most is happy death,
which is absolutely painless
and full of bustle, excitement
and even dramatic spectacle.

zh: 自己很难控制，即很难控制在一定的范围之内。
en:
It is difficult to exercise self-control,
that is, difficult to keep within limits.

zh: 因为我觉得喝酒不一定完全是坏事，少喝一点可以舒筋活血，据说对心血管也是有帮助的。
en:
Drinking is, to my mind,
not always bad
because a few spots
may help blood circulation
and is, as they say,
good for the heart and blood vessels.

zh: 作家不能当隐士，适当的社会活动和文学活动可以开阔眼界，活跃思想，对创作也是有帮助的。
en:
Being no hermit,
a writer stands to benefit in writing
as long as he gets properly involved with
social and literary activities
to widen his field of vision
and stimulate his thinking.

zh: 可是怎么才能不酗酒、不作酒鬼，这有益的定量究竟是多少呢？
en:
But how can he
avoid excessive drinking
or becoming of drunkard?
What is the safety limit
in this respect?

zh: 怕就怕三杯下肚，豪情大发，嘟嘟嘟，来个瓶底朝天，
en:
The trouble is after three cups of alcohol
he will get wild and unrestrained
and end in gulping down a whole bottle.

zh: 而且一顿喝不上便情绪不高，颇有怨言，甚至会到处去找酒喝。
en:
One meal without liquor will upset him
and set him complaining
and searching around for drink.

zh: 呜呼，快乐地死去！
en: Alas,just to end up dying happily!

zh: 学问与趣味 梁实秋
en: Learning and Personal Inclination Liang Shiqiu

zh: 前辈的学者常以学问的趣味启迪后生，
en:
Scholars of the older generation
often urge young people to
develop interest in learning

zh: 因为他们自己实在是得到了学问的趣味，
en:
because they themselves
have been enjoying
the real pleasure of academic studies.

zh: 故不惜现身说法，诱导后学，
en:
And they are ever ready to
cite their own example
by way of advice,

zh: 使他们也在愉快的心情之下走进学问的大门。
en:
in hopes of enabling young people
to gain access to scholarship
in an enjoyable way.

zh: 例如，梁任公先生就说过：
en:
For example,
the distinguished scholar Liang Qichao
once said wittily,

zh: 我是个主张趣味主义的人，
en:
I always stand for interest-ism. ★两个小词：
stand for代表；为…而奋斗；拥护
interest-ism 趣味主义
★趣味主义：译为interest-ism,其中“-ism”乃表达“主义”而采用的英语后缀。
“Dengism”→邓小平理论；“Maoism”→毛泽东思想；“Marxism”→马克思主义连这句了三个例子，可算是清楚了吧？“XXX-ism”就是“XXX思想/主义/等等”。
19 倘若用化学化分梁启超’这件东西，
把里头所含一种原素名叫‘趣味’的抽出来， If you broke down Liang Qichao's stuff
into its component parts, 如果你将梁启超这个东西打碎，
分解成许多小块块。 ★倘若用化学化分梁启超’这件东西：译为 If you broke down Liang Qichao's stuff into its component parts,其中短语动词 broke down 意即“分解”（to decompose),例如 Water can be broken down into hydrogen and oxygen。
★component part:“component”是成分，“part”也是表示部分，部分的部分就真的是分解的很碎了。
component n.成分；零件；[数]要素；组分；
19 只怕所剩下的仅有个零了。 there would be nothing left
except an element named 'interest'.

zh: 任公先生注重趣味，学问甚是渊博，
en:
Mr. Liang was a man of profound learning
who attached much importance to interest.

zh: 而并不存有任何外在的动机，只是“无所为而为”，故能有他那样的成就。
en:
He attained great academic success
because he pursued scholarly study solely
for its own sake,
without any ulterior motive.

zh: 一个人在学问上果能感觉到趣味，有时真会像是着了魔一般，
en:
A man who is really interested in learning
sometimes does act like one possessed.

zh: 真能废寝忘食，真能不知老之将至，苦苦钻研，镶而不舍，在学问上焉能不有收获？
en:
He forgets his approaching old age
and works hard even to
the neglect of his meals and sleep.
Isn't it but natural
for a man of such devotion
to have great scholarly achievements?

zh: 不过我尝想，以任公先生而论，他后期的著述如历史研究法，先秦政治思想史，以及有关墨子佛学陶渊明的作品，
en:
But, though Mr. Liang's later works,
such as those on method of historical studies,
political and ideological history of the pre-Qin days,
as well as those on Mohism,
Buddhism and Tao Yuanming,

zh: 都可说是他的一点“趣味”在驱使着他，
en:
were motivated by
his personal inclination,

zh: 可是在他在年青的时候，从师受业，诵读典籍，那时节也全然是趣味么？
en:
can the same be said of his younger days
when he was a pupil
chanting ancient Chinese books
under a private tutor?

zh: 作八文，作试帖诗，莫非也是趣味么？我想未必。
en:
Was he motivated by his personal inclination
while learning to write stereotyped essays
and poems prescribed for
the imperials civil service examinations?
No, I think not.

zh: 大概趣味云云，是指年长之后自动/作学问之时/而言，在年青时候/为学问打根底之际/恐怕不能过分重视趣味。
en:
Generally speaking,
the so-called interest begins to exist
only when one is mature enough
to engage in independent studies.
It is improper, I am afraid,
for young people to over stress
the importance of interest
while they are still in
the period of learning the basics of knowledge.

zh: 学问没有根底，趣味也很难滋生。
en:
Interest will never develop where no solid foundation
has been laid for learning.

zh: 任公先生的学问之所以那样的博大精深，涉笔成趣，左右逢源，不能不说的一大部分得力于他的学问根底之打得坚固。
en:
There is no denying the fact that
Mr. Liang owed his
wide erudition and unusual literary talent,
for the most part,
to his good grasp of foundation knowledge.

zh:
我尝见许多年青的朋友，聪明用功，成绩优异，
而语文程度不足以达意，甚至写一封信亦难得通顺，
问其故则曰其兴趣不在语文方面。
先别急，容我大白话来一遍：
【我曾经见过许多年轻的朋友，他们聪明用功，成绩优异
不过语文成都不能传文达意，甚至写信都写不通顺，
问他为什么？他就说他的兴趣不在语文上。】
en:
I have come across a great many
bright and diligent young friends
who have done exceedingly well
in their studies,
but are rather weak in Chinese.
They cannot even write a letter
in correct Chinese.
When I asked them why,
they said they were
not interested in the Chinese language.

zh: 又有一些位，执笔为文，斐然可诵，而视数理科如仇兽，勉强才能及格，
en:
