but he still wants to work
to save up for a house
to be built for me,

zh: 一个朋友从北方来，告诉了我这样的话。
en: a friend of mine from North China told me.

zh: 他的话使我想起了我的父亲。我的父亲正是和他的父亲完全一样的。
en:
That put me in mind of my father.
My father was very much like his.

zh: 我的父亲曾经为我苦了一生，
en:
Father went through
untold hardships for me all his life.

zh: 把我养大，送我进学校，为我造了屋子，买了几亩田地。
en:
He brought me up,
sent me to school,
had a house built for me
and bought me a few mu of land。

zh: 六十岁那一年，还到汉口去做生意，怕人家嫌他年老，只说自己五十几岁。
en:
He went to Hankou to engage in trade
the year when he was already sixty.
And he tried to make out
that he was still in his fifties
lest people should consider him
too old to be of much use.

zh: 大家都劝他不要再出门，他偏背着包裹走了。
en:
We had all tried to
dissuade him from going out to Hankou,
but he simply wouldn't listen and left home
carrying the luggage on his back.

zh: “让我再帮儿子几年！”他只是这样说。
en:
Let me toil a few more years
for my son's sake!
That was what he said.

zh: 后来屋子被火烧掉了，他还想再做生意，把屋子重造起来。
en:
It happened afterwards
that the house was burned down.
And he wanted to go back to his business
in order to have the house rebuilt.

zh: 我安慰他说，三年以后我自己就可积起钱造屋了，还是等一等吧。
en:
I tried to console him,
saying that there was no need
for him to do it
because in three years' time
I myself would have laid by
enough money for a new house.

zh: 他答应了。
en: He agreed.

zh: 他给我留下了许多造屋的材料，告诉我这样可以做什么那样可以做什么。
en:
Then he gave me a lot of building materials|
and told me what to do with them.

zh: 他死的以前不久，还对我说：“早一点造起来吧，我可以给你监工。”
en:
Shortly before his death, he urged me,
"You'd better get started right away
so that I can watch to see
that everything is done properly."

zh: 但是他终于没有看见屋子重造起来就死了。他弥留的时候对我说，一切都满足了。
en:
Unfortunately he didn't
live long enough
to see the new house.
He told me on his death bed
that had nothing to feel sorry about.

zh: 但是我知道他倘能再活几年，我把屋子造起来，是他所最心愿的。
en:
But I knew he would be much happier
if he could live a few more years
just to see the new house put up.

zh: 我听他弥留时的呻吟和叹息。我知道他还想再活几年，帮我造起屋子来。
en:
When I heard his dying groans and sighs,
I believed they were
caused not by physical pain,
but by regret for
not being able to live a few more years
to help me with the new house.

zh: 现在我自己已是几个孩子的父亲了。我爱孩子，但我没有像前一辈父亲的想法，帮孩子一直帮到老，帮到死还不足。
en:
Now I myself am
a father of several children.
Though I love my kids,
I do not share the idea of
father and people of his time
that one can never do
too much in his lifetime
to help his children.

zh: 我赞美前一辈父亲的美德，而自己却不跟着他们的步伐走去。
en:
Much as I admire
father and people of his time
for their moral excellence,
I can never follow in their footsteps.

zh: 我觉得我的孩子累我，使我受到极大的束缚。
en: I think of my children as an encumbrance to me.

zh: 我没有对他们永久的计划，甚至连短促的也没有。
en:
I haven't worked out
a long-term plan for them,
nay,not even a short-term one.

zh:
“倘使有人要，我愿意把他们送给人家！”
我常常这样说，当我厌恶孩子的时候。
en:
I'd like to give away my kids to anyone
who's willing to take them!
That's what I say
whenever I am fed up with them.

zh: 唉，和前一辈做父亲的一比，我觉得我们这一辈生命力薄弱得可怜，
en:
Alas, compared with
father and people of his time,
the present generation, I think,
have pitifully low vitality.

zh: 我们二三十岁的前辈，他们虽然老的老死的死了，但是他们才是真正活着到现在到将来。
en:
We in our twenties or thirties
cannot compare with
our elders in their sixties or seventies.
Today they may be advanced in years or even no more,
but they will, nevertheless, live forever and ever.

zh: 而我们呢，虽然活着，却是早已死了。
en: As for us, though still alive, we have long been dead.

zh: 我与父亲不相见已二年余了，我最不能忘记的是他的背影。
en:
It is more than two years
since I last saw father,
and what I can never forget
is the sight of his back.

zh: 那年冬天，祖母死了，父亲的差使也交卸了，正是祸不单行的日子，我从北京到徐州，打算跟着父亲奔丧回家。
en:
Misfortunes never come singly.
In the winter of more than two years ago,
grandma died and father lost his job.
I left Beijing for Xuzhou
to join father in hastening home
to attend grandma's funeral.

zh: 到了徐州见着父亲，看见满院狼藉的东西，又想起祖母，不禁策策地流下眼泪。
en:
When I met father in Xuzhou,
the sight of the disorderly mess
in his courtyard
and the thought of grandma
started tears trickling down my cheeks.

zh: 父亲说：“事已如此，不必难过，好在天无绝人之路！”
en:
Father said,
"Now that things've come to such a pass,
it's no use crying. Fortunately,
Heaven always leaves one a way out."

zh: 回家变卖典质，父亲还了亏空；又借了钱办了丧事。
en:
After arriving home in Yangzhou,
father paid off debts
by selling or pawning things.
He also borrowed money
to meet the funeral expenses.

zh: 这些日子，家中光景很是惨淡，一半为了丧事，一半为了父亲的赋闲。
en:
Between grandma's funeral
and father's unemployment,
our family was then
in reduced circumstances.

zh: 丧事完毕，父亲要到南京谋事，我也要回到北京念书，我们便同行。
en:
After the funeral was over,
father was to go to Nanjing to look for a job
and I was to return to Beijing to study,
so we started out together.

zh: 到南京时，有朋友约去游逛，勾留了一日；第二日上午便须渡江到浦口，下午上车北去。
en:
I spent the first day in Nanjing
strolling about with some friends
at their invitation,
and was ferrying across the Yangtse River
to Pukou the next morning
and thence taking a train for Beijing
on the afternoon of the same day.

zh: 父亲因为事忙，本已说定不送我，叫旅馆里一个熟识的茶房陪我同去。
en:
Father said he was too busy to
go and see me off at the railway station,
but would ask a hotel waiter that he knew
to accompany me there instead.

zh: 但他终于不放心，怕茶房不妥贴，颇踌躇了一会。他再三嘱咐茶房，甚是仔细。
en:
He urged the waiter again and again
to take good care of me,
but still did not quite trust him.
He hesitated for quite a while
about what to do.

zh: 其实那年我已二十岁，北京来往过两三次，是没有甚么要紧的了。
en:
As a matter of fact,
nothing would matter at all
because I was then twenty
and had already travelled
on Beijing-Pukou Railway
a couple of times.

zh: 他踌躇了一会，终于决定还是自己送我去。
en:
After some wavering, he finally decided that
he himself would accompany me to the station.

zh: 我两三回劝他不必去；他只说，“不要紧，他们去不好！”
en:
I repeatedly tried to talk him out of it,
but he only said, "Never mind!
It won't do to trust
guys like those hotel boys!"

zh: 我们过了江，进了车站。我买票，他忙着照看行李。
en:
We entered the railway station
after crossing the River.
While I was at the booking office
buying a ticket,
father saw to my luggage.

zh: 行李太多了，得向脚夫行些小费，才可过去。他便又忙着和他们讲价钱。
en:
There was quite a bit of luggage
and he had to bargain
with the porter over the fee.

zh: 我那时真是太聪明过分，总觉得他说话不大漂亮，非得自己插嘴不可。
en:
I was then such a smart aleck
that I frowned upon
the way father was haggling
and was on the verge of
chipping in a few words
when the bargain was finally clinched.

zh: 但他终于讲定了价钱；就送我上车。他给我拣定了靠车门的一张椅子；我将他给我做的紫毛大衣铺好坐位。
en:
Getting on the train with me,
he picked me a seat
close to the carriage door.
I spread on the seat
the brownish fur-lined overcoat
he had got tailor made for me.

zh: 他嘱我路上小心，夜里要警醒些，不要受凉。又嘱托茶房好好照应我。
en:
He told me to be watchful on the way
and be careful not to catch cold at night.
he also asked the train attendants
to take good care of me.

zh: 我心里暗笑他的迁；他们只认得钱，托他们直是白托！
en:
I sniggered at father
for being so impractical,
for it was utterly useless
to entrust me to those attendants,
who cared for nothing but money.

zh: 而且我这样大年纪的人，难道还不能料理自己吗？唉，我现在想想，那时真是太聪明了！
en:
Besides, it was certainly no problem
for a person of my age to look after himself.
Oh, when I come to think of it,
I can see how smarty I was in those days!

zh: 我说道，“爸爸，你走吧。”他望车外看了看，说，“我买几个橘子去。你就在此地，不要走动。”
en:
I said, "Dad, you might leave now."
But he looked out of window and said,
"I'm going to buy you some tangerines.
You just stay here. Don't move around."

zh: 我看那边月台的栅栏外有几个卖东西的等着顾客。
en:
I caught sight of several vendors
waiting for customers
outside the railings
beyond a platform.

zh: 走到那边月台，须穿过铁道，须跳下去又爬上去。父亲是一个胖子，走过去自然要费些事。
en:
But to reach that platform
would require crossing the railway track
and doing some climbing up and down.
That would be a strenuous job for father,
who was fat.

zh: 我本来要去的，他不肯，只好让他去。
en:
I wanted to do all that myself,
but he stopped me,
so I could do nothing but let him go.

zh: 我看见他戴着黑布小帽，穿着黑布大马褂，深青布棉袍，瞒踞在走到铁道边，
en:
I watched him hobble
towards the railway track
in his black skullcap,
black cloth mandarin jacket
and dark blue cotton-padded cloth long gown.

zh:
慢慢探身下去，尚不大难。
可是他穿过铁道，要爬上那边月台，就不容易了。
en:
He had little trouble
climbing down the railway track,
but it was a lot more difficult for him
to climb up that platform
after crossing the railway track.

zh: 他用两手攀着上面，两脚再向上缩；他肥胖的身子向左微倾，显出努力的样子。
en:
His hands held onto
the upper part of the platform,
his legs huddled up
and his corpulent body
tipped slightly towards the left,
obviously making an enormous exertion.

zh: 这时我看见他的的背影，我眼泪很快地流下来了。
en:
While I was watching him from behind,
tears gushed from my eyes.

zh: 我赶紧拭干了泪，怕他看见，也怕别人看见。
en:
I quickly wiped them away
lest he or others should catch me crying.

zh: 我再向外看时，他已抱了朱红的橘子往回走了。
en:
The next moment
when I looked out of the window again,
father was already on the way back,
holding bright red tangerines in both hands.

zh: 过铁道时，他先将橘子散放在地上，自己慢慢爬下，再抱起橘子走。
en:
In crossing the railway track,
he first put the tangerines on the ground,
climbed down slowly
and then picked them up again.

zh:
到这边时，我赶紧去掺他。他和我走到车上，将橘子一股脑儿放在我的皮大衣
上。于是扑扑衣上泥土，心里很轻松似的，过了一会说，“我走了，到那边来信！”
en:
When he came near the train,
I hurried out to help him by the hand.
After boarding the train with me,
he laid all the tangerines on my overcoat,
and patting the dirt off his clothes,
he looked somewhat relieved
and said after a while,
"I must be going now.
Donapos;t forget to write me from Beijing!”

zh: 我望着他走出去。他走了几步，回过头看见我，说，“进去吧，里边没人。”
en:
I gazed after his back
retreating out of the carriage.
After a few steps,
he looked back at me and said,
"go back to your seat.
Don't leave your things alone.”

zh:
等他的背影混入来来往往的人里，再找不着了，
我便进来坐下，我的眼泪又来了。
en:
I, however, did not go back to my seat
until his figure was lost among
crowds of people hurrying to and fro
and no longer visible.
My eyes were again wet with tears.

zh: 近几年来，父亲和我都是东奔西走，家中的光景是一日不如一日。
en:
In recent years, both father and I
have been living an unsettled life,
and the circumstances of our family
going from bad to worse.

zh: 他少年出外谋生，独力支持，做了许多大事。
en:
Father left home to seek
a livelihood when young
and did achieve quite a few things
all on his own.

zh: 那知老境却如此颓唐！
en:
To think that he should now
be so downcast in old age!

zh: 他触目伤怀，自然不能自己。情郁于中，自然要发之于外；
en:
The discouraging state of affairs
filled him with
an uncontrollable feeling of deep sorrow,
and his pent-up emotion had to find a vent.

zh: 家庭琐屑便往往触他之怒。他待我渐渐不同往日。
en:
That is why even mere domestic trivialities
would often make him angry,
and meanwhile
he became less and less nice with me.

zh: 但最近两年的不见，他终于忘却我的不好，只是惦记着我，惦记着我的儿子。
en:
However, the separation of the last two years
has made him more forgiving towards me.
He keeps thinking about me and my son.

zh: 我北来后，他写了一信给我，信中说道，“我身体平安，惟膀子疼痛利害，举署提笔，诸多不便，大约大去之期不远矣。”
en:
After I arrived in Beijing, he wrote me a letter,
in which he says."I'm all right except for
a severe pain in my arm.
I even have trouble using
chopsticks or writing brushes.
Perhaps it won't be long now
before I depart this life."

zh: 我读到此处，在晶莹的泪光中，又看见那肥胖的，青布马褂的背影。唉！我不知何时再能与他相见！
en:
Through the glistening tears
which these words had brought to my eyes
I again saw the back of father's corpulent form
in the dark blue cotton-padded cloth long gown
and the black cloth mandarin jacket.
Oh, how I long to see him again.

zh: 二十年来，我的生活费中至少十分之一二是消耗在书上的。我的房子里比较贵重的东西就是书。
en:
For twenty years past,
books have eaten into
at least 10-20 percent of my pocket.
Now the only things of some value
under my roof, if any, are my books.

zh: 我一向没有对于任何问题作高深研究的野心，因之所以买的书范围较广，宗教、艺术、文学、社会、哲学、历史、生物，各方面差不多都有一点。
en:
Since I have never entertained ambition for
making a profound study of any subject,
the books I have acquired
cover almost everything
--religion, art, literature, sociology,
philosophy, history, biology, etc.

zh: 最多的是各国文学名著的译本，与本国古来的诗文集，别的门类只是些概论等类的入门书而已。
en:
Most of them are Chinese translations
of literary works by famous foreign writers and anthologies of Chinese poetry and prose through the ages.
The rest, often called an outline or introduction,
are merely on rudiments of various subjects.

zh: 我不喜欢向别人或图书馆借书。借来的书，在我好像过不来瘾似的，必要是自己买的才满足。这也可谓是一种占有的欲望。
en:
I never care to borrow books
from other people or a library.
It seems that books bought can better satisfy my bibliomania
than books borrowed.
You may also attribute this
to some sort of desire
for personal possession.

zh: 买到了几册新书，一册一册在加盖藏书印记，我最感到快悦的是这时候。
en:
Whenever I have some new acquisitions,
it always gives me
great pleasure and satisfaction
to stamp my ex-libris on them one by one.

zh: 书籍到了我的手里，我的习惯是先看序文，次看目录。
en:
As soon as a new book comes to hand,
I always read the preface first
and then the table of contents.

zh: 页数不多的往往立刻通读，篇幅大的，只把正文任择一二章节略加翻阅，就插在书架上。
en:
If it happens to be a thin one,
I often finish reading it at one sitting.
Otherwise, I often browse through
one or two chapters or sections
before putting it onto my bookshelf.

zh: 除小说外，我少有全体读完的大部的书，
en:
I seldom read a thick book
from cover to cover
unless it is a novel.

zh: 只凭了购入当时的记忆，知道某册书是何种性质，其中大概有些什么可取的材料而已。
en:
By dint of the first impression
it made on me
at the time of buying,
I have a rough idea of
what a book is about
and what useful materials in it
are available to me.

zh: 什么书在什么时候再去读再去翻，连我自己也无把握，(前废后主）完全要看一个时期一个时期的兴趣。
en:
But I have little idea
which book is to be read
or looked over again at what time.
It is completely subject to
the whims of the moment.

zh: 关于这事，我常自比为古时的皇帝，而把插在架上的书籍诸列屋而居的宫女。
en:
This often prompts me to liken myself
and the books on my shelves
respectively to an ancient emperor
and his concubines housed separately
in a row of adjoining rooms.

zh: 我虽爱买书，而对于书却不甚爱惜。
en:
Much as I love books,
I take little care of them.

zh: 读书的时候，常在书上把我认为要紧的处所标出。
en:
In doing my reading,
I often mark out
what I regard as important
in a book.

zh: 线装书大概用笔加圈，洋装书竟用红铅笔划粗粗的线。
en:
If it is a thread-bound Chinese book,
I use a writing brush
to draw small circles as markings.
Otherwise,
I use a red pencil
to draw heavy underlines.

zh: 经我看过的书，统体干净的很少。
en:
Consequently,
the books I have read
are rarely clean.

zh: 据说，任何爱吃糖果的人，只要叫他到糖果铺中去做事，见了糖果就会生厌。
en:
It is said that
those who have a great liking for candies
will sicken to see them
when later they happen to
work in a candy store.

zh: 自我入书店以后，对于书的贪念也已消除了不少了，可不免要故态复萌，想买这种，想买那种。
en:
Likewise, ever since I began to
work in a bookstore,
my obsession with books
has been very much on the decline.
Nevertheless,
I still can not help
slipping back into the same old rut,
eager to buy this and that book.

zh: 这大概因为糖果要用嘴去吃，摆存毫无意义，而书则可以买了不看，任其只管插在架上的缘故吧。
en:
This is probably because
candies are to be eaten with the mouth
and not worth keeping as knick-knacks
while books can be bought
without being read
and just left on a shelf.

zh: 秋天，无论在什么地方的秋天，总是好的；
en:
Autumn, wherever it is,
always has something
to recommend itself.

zh: 可是啊，北国的秋，却特别地来得清，来得静，来得悲凉。
en:
In North China, however,
it is particularly limpid,
serene and melancholy.

zh: 我的不远千里，要从杭州赶上青岛，更要从青岛赶上北平来的理由，也不过想饱尝一尝这“秋”，这故都的秋味。
en:
To enjoy its atmosphere to the full
in the onetime capital,
I have, therefore,
made light of travelling a long distance
from Hanghou to Qingdao,
and thence to Peiping.

zh: 江南，秋当然也是有的，但草木凋得慢，空气来得润，天的颜色显得淡，并且又时常多雨而少风；
en:
There is of course autumn in the South too,
but over there plants wither slowly,
the air is moist, the sky pallid,
and it is more often rainy than windy.

zh:
一个人夹在苏州上海杭州，或厦门香港广州的市民中间，浑浑沌沌地过去，只能感到一点点清凉，
秋的味，秋的色，秋的意境与姿态，总看不饱，尝不透，赏玩不到十足。
en:
While muddling along all by myself
among the urban dwellers of Suzhou, Shanghai,
Xianmen, Hong Kong or Guangzhou,
I feel nothing but a little chill in the air,
without ever relishing to
my heart's content the flavour, colour,
mood and style of the season.

zh: 秋并不是名花，也并不是美酒，那一种半开，半醉的状态，在领略秋的过程上，是不合适的。
en:
Unlike famous flowers
which are most attractive
when half opening,
good wine
which is most tempting
when one is half drunk,
autumn, however,
is best appreciated in its entirety.

zh: 不逢北国之秋，已将近十余年了。
en:
It is more than a decade
since I last saw autumn in North.

zh: 在南方每年到了秋天，总要想陶然亭的芦花，钓鱼台的柳影，西山的虫唱，玉泉的夜月，潭拓寺的钟声。
en:
When I am in the South,
the arrival of each autumn
will put me in mind of
Peiping's Tao Ran Ting with its reed catkins,
Diao Yu Tai with its shady willow trees,
Western Hills with their chirping insects,
Yu Quan Shan Mountain on a moonlight evening
and Tan Zhe Si with its reverberating bell.

zh: 在北平即使不出门去罢，就是在皇城人海之中，租人家一橡破屋来住着，早晨起来，泡一碗浓茶，向院子一坐，你也能看到很高很高的碧绿的天色，听得到青天下驯鸽的飞声。
en:
Suppose you put up in
a humble rented house
inside the bustling imperial city,
you can, on getting up at dawn,
sit in your courtyard
sipping a cup of strong tea,
leisurely watch the high azure skies
and listen to pigeons circling overhead.

zh: 从槐树叶底，朝东细数着一丝一丝漏下来的日光，
en:
Turn eastward under locust trees
to closely observe streaks of sunlight
filtering through their foliage,

zh: 或在破壁腰中，静对着像喇叭似的牵牛花（朝荣）的蓝朵，自然而然地也能感觉到十分的秋意。
en:
or quietly watch
the trumpet-shaped blue flowers
of morning glories
climbing half way up a dilapidated wall,
and an intense feeling of autumn
will of itself well up inside you.

zh: 说到牵牛花，我以为以蓝色或白色者为佳，紫黑色次之，淡红色最下。
en:
As to morning glories,
I like their blue or white flowers best,
dark purple ones second best,
and pink ones third best.

zh: 最好，还要在牵牛花底教长着几根疏疏落落的尖细且长的秋草，使作陪衬。
en:
It will be most desirable
to have them set off
by some tall thin grass
planted underneath here and there.

zh: 北国的槐树，也是一种能使人联想起秋来的点缀。
en:
Locust trees in the North,
as a decorative embellishment of nature,
also associate us with autumn.

zh: 像花而又不是花的那一种落蕊，早晨起来，会铺得满地。
en:
On getting up early in the morning,
you will find the ground
strewn all over with flower-like pistils
fallen from locust trees.

zh: 脚踏上去，声音也没有，气味也没有，只能感出一点点极微细极柔软的触觉。
en:
Quiet and smelless,
they feel tiny and soft underfoot.

zh: 扫街在树影下一阵扫后，灰土上留下来的一条条扫帚的丝纹，看起来既觉得细腻，又觉得清闲，潜意识下并且还觉得有点儿落寞，
en:
After a street cleaner has done the sweeping
under the shade of the trees,
you will discover countless lines
left by his broom in the dust,
which look so fine and quiet
that somehow a feeling of forlorness
will begin to creep up on you.

zh: 古人所说的梧桐一叶而天下知秋的遥想，大约也就在这些深沉的地方。
en:
The same depth of implication
is found in the ancient saying
that a single fallen leaf from the wutong tree
is more than enough to
inform the world of autumn's presence.

zh: 秋蝉的衰弱的残声，更是北国的特产；
en:
The sporadic feeble chirping of cicadas
is especially characteristic of
autumn in the North.

zh: 因为北平处处全长着树，屋子又低，所以无论在什么地方，都听得见它们的啼唱。
en:
Due to the abundance of trees
and the low altitude of dwellings in Peiping,
cicadas are audible
in every nook and cranny of the city.

zh: 在南方是非要上郊外或山上去才听得到的。
en:
In the South, however,
one cannot hear them
unless in suburbs or hills.

zh: 这秋蝉的嘶叫，在北平可和蟋蟀耗子一样，简直像是家家户户都养在家里的家虫。
en:
Because of their ubiquitous shrill noise,
these insects in Peiping
seem to be living off every household
like crickets or mice.

zh: 还有秋雨哩，北方的秋雨，也似乎比南方的下得奇，下得有味，下得更像样。
en:
As for autumn rains in the North,
they also seem to
differ from those in the South,
being more appealing, more temperate.

zh: 在灰沉沉的天底下，忽而来一阵凉风，便息列索落地下起雨来了。
en:
A sudden gust of cool wind
under the slaty sky,
and raindrops will start
pitter-pattering.

zh: 一层雨过，云渐渐地卷向了西去，天又青了，太阳又露出脸来了；
en:
Soon when the rain is over,
the clouds begin gradually
to roll towards the west
and the sun comes out in the blue sky.

zh: 著着很厚的青布单衣或夹袄的都市闲人，咬着烟管，在雨后的斜桥影里，上桥头树底下去一立，遇见熟人，便会用了缓慢悠闲的声调，微叹着互答着说：
en:
Some idle townsfolk,
wearing lined or unlined clothing
made of thick cloth,
will come out pipe in mouth and,
loitering under a tree by the end of a bridge,
exchange leisurely conversation with acquaintances
with a slight touch of regret at the passing of time:

zh:
“唉，天可真凉了——”
“可不是么？一层秋雨一层凉了！”
en:
Oh, real nice and cool-
"Sure! Getting cooler
with each autumn shower!"

zh: 北方的果树，到秋来，也是一种奇景。
en:
Fruit trees in the North
also make a wonderful sight
in autumn.

zh: 第一是枣子树；屋角，墙头，茅房边上，灶房门口，它都会一株株地长大起来。
en:
Take jujube tree for example.
They grow everywhere-
around the corner of a house,
at the foot of a wall,
by the side of a latrine
or outside a kitchen door.

zh:
像橄榄又像鸽蛋似的这枣子颗儿，
在小椭圆形的细叶中间，显出淡绿微黄的颜色的时候，正是秋的全盛时期；
en:
It is at the height of autumn
that jujubes, shaped like dates or pigeon eggs,
make their appearance
in a light yellowish-green
amongst tiny elliptic leaves.

zh: 等枣树叶落，枣子红完，西北风就要起来了，北方便是尘沙灰土的世界，
en:
By the time when they have
turned ruddy and the leaves fallen,
the north-westerly wind will begin to reign supreme
and make a dusty world of the North.

zh: 只有这枣子、柿子、葡萄，成熟到八九分的七八月之交，是北国的清秋的佳日，是一年之中最好也没有的 golden days。
en:
Only at the turn of July and August
when jujubes, persimmons, grapes
are80-90 percent ripe
will the North have the best of autumn
——the golden days in a year.

zh: 有些批评家说，中国的文人学士，尤其是诗人，都带着很浓厚的颓废色彩，所以中国的诗文里，颂赞秋的文字特别的多。
en:
Some literary critics say that
Chinese literati, especially poets,
are mostly disposed to be decadent,
which accounts for
predominance of Chinese works
singing the praises of autumn.

zh: 但外国的诗人，又何尝不然？
en: Well, the same is true of foreign poets, isn't it?

zh: 我虽则外国诗文念得不多，也不想开账来，做一篇秋的诗歌散文钞，
en:
I haven't read much of
foreign poetry and prose,
nor do I want to enumerate
autumn-related poems and essays
in foreign literature.

zh:
但你若去一翻英德法意等诗人的集子，或各国的诗文的anthology来，
总能够看到许多关于秋的歌颂与悲啼。
en:
But, if you browse through collected works
of English, German, French or Italian poets,
or various countries'anthologies of poetry or prose,
you can always comes across a great many
literary pieces eulogizing or lamenting autumn.

zh:
各著名的大诗人的长篇田园诗或四季诗里，
也总以关于秋的部分，写得最出色而最有味。
en:
Long pastoral poems
or songs about the four seasons
by renowned poets
are mostly distinguished by
beautiful moving lines on autumn.

zh:
足见有感觉的动物，有情趣的人类，
对于秋，总是一样的能特别引起深沉，幽远，严厉，萧索的感触来的。
en:
All that goes to show that
all live creatures and sensitive humans alike
are prone to the feeling of
depth, remoteness, severity and bleakness.

zh: 不单是诗人，就是被关闭在牢狱里的囚犯，到了秋天，我想也一定会感到一种不能自己的深情；
en:
Not only poets,
even convicts in prison, I suppose,
have deep sentiments in autumn
in spite of themselves.

zh: 秋之于人，何尝有国别，更何尝有人种阶级的区别呢？
en:
Autumn treats all humans alike,
regardless of nationality,race or class.

zh: 不过在中国，文字里有一个“秋士”的成语，读本里又有着很普遍的欧阳子的秋声与苏东坡的《赤壁赋》等，就觉得中国的文人，与秋的关系特别深了。
en:
However, judging from Chinese idiom qiushi
(autumn scholar, meaning an aged scholar
grieving over frustrations in his life)
and frequent selection in textbooks of
Ouyang Xiu's On the Autumn Sough
and Su Dongpo's On the Red Cliff,
Chinese men of letters
seem to be particularly autumn-minded.

zh: 可是这秋的深味，非要在北方，才感受得到底。
en:
But, to know the real flavour of autumn,
especially China's autumn,
one has to visit the North.

zh: 南国之秋，当然是也有它的特异的地方的，
en:
Autumn in the South
also has its unique features,

zh: 比如廿四桥的明月，钱塘江的秋潮，普陀山的凉雾，荔枝湾的残荷等等，可是色彩不浓，回味不永。
en:
such as the moonlit Ershisi Bridge in Yangzhou,
the flowing sea tide at the Qiantangjiang River,
the mist-shrouded Putuo Mountain
and lotuses at the Lizhiwan Bay.
But they all lack strong colour and lingering flavour.

zh: 比起北国的秋来，正像是黄酒之于白干，稀饭之于馍漠，鲈鱼之于大蟹，黄犬之于骆驼。
en:
Southern autumn is to Northern autumn
what yellow rice wine is to kaoliang wine,
congee to steamed buns,
perches to crabs,
yellow dogs to camels.

zh: 秋天，这北国的秋天，若留得往的话，我愿把寿命的三分之二折去，换得一个三分之一的零头。
en:
Autumn, I mean Northern autumn,
if only it could be made to last forever!
I would be more than willing to
keep but one-third of my life-span
and have two-thirds of it bartered for
the prolonged stay of the season!

zh: 永远的憧憬和追求 萧红
en: My Everlasting Dream and Pursuit Xiao Hong

zh:
一九一一年，在一个小县城里边，我生在一个小地主的家里。
那县城差不多就是中国的最东最北部——黑龙江省——所以一年之中，倒有四个月飘着白雪。
en:
In 1911, I was born into
a petty Landlord family
in a remote county town
in Heilongjiang Province
——a town situated virtually at
the northeastern tip of China.
We had snow there
for as long as one third of a year.

zh: 父亲常常为着贪婪而失掉了人性。
en:
Father, driven by avarice,
often became very unfeeling.

zh: 他对待仆人，对待自己的儿女，以及对待我的祖父都是同样的吝啬而疏远，甚至于无情。
en:
He would treat his servants,
his own children
and even my grandpa alike
with meanness and indifference,
not to say with ruthlessness.

zh: 有一次，为着房屋租金的事情，父亲把房客的全套的马车赶了过来。
en:
Once,due to a dispute over house rent,
he took away by force
a tenant's horse-drawn cart
and drove it home.

zh: 房客的家属们哭着诉说着，向我的祖父跪了下来，于是祖父把两匹棕色的马从车上解下来还了回去。
en:
The tenant's family
came to see grandpa and,
dropping to their knees,
tearfully related their troubles.
Grandpa unharnessed
the two chestnut horses
and returned them to tenant.

zh: 为着这匹马，父亲向祖父起着终夜的争吵。
en:
That touched off
a night-long quarrel
between father and grandpa.

zh:
“两匹马，咱们是算不了什么的，穷人，这匹马就是命根。”
祖父这样说着，而父亲还是争吵。
en:
The two horses mean nothing to us,
but everything to the poor,
argued grandpa.
Father, however, refused to listen.

zh: 九岁时，母亲死去。
en: Mother died when I was nine.

zh: 父亲也就更变了样，偶然打碎了一只杯子，他就要骂到使人发抖的程度。
en:
From then on
father went from bad to worse.
Even a mere cup
accidentally broken by someone
would send him into such a violent rage
that we all shivered with fear.

zh: 后来就连父亲的眼睛也转了弯，每从他的身边经过，我就像自己的身上生了针刺一样；
en:
Later, whenever I happened to
walk past him,
he would even have his eyes
directed sideways,
which made me feel like
being pricked all over on thorns!

zh: 他斜视着你，他那高傲的眼光从鼻梁经过嘴角而后往下流着。
en:
When he looked askance at me,
superciliousness gushed from his eyes
down the bridge of his nose
and then off the corners of his mouth.

zh: 所以每每在大雪中的黄昏里，围着暖炉，围着祖父，听着祖父读着诗篇，看着祖父读着诗篇时微红的嘴唇。
en:
Often of a snowy evening,
we children would hang about grandpa
by a heating stove,
listening to him reading poems aloud
and meanwhile watching his busy ruddy lips.

zh: 父亲打了我的时候，我就在祖父的房里，一直面向着窗子，从黄昏到深夜——窗外的白雪，好像白棉花一样飘着；而暖炉上水壶的盖子，则像伴奏的乐器似的振动着。
en:
Whenever father had given me a beating,
I would seek solace in grandpa's room
where I would stay
gazing out of the window
from dusk till late into the night
while snowflakes were flying like cotton
and the lid of the kettle
over the heating stove
rattling like a musical instrument
playing an accompaniment.

zh: 祖父时时把多纹的两手放在我的肩上，而后又放在我头上，我的耳边便响着这样的声音：“快快长吧！长大就好了。”
en:
Grandpa would place his wrinkled hand
on my shoulder
and then on my head, saying,
" Grow up quick, poor child!
You'll be all right
after you've grown up."

zh: 二十岁那年，我就逃出了父亲的家庭。直到现在还是过着流浪的生活。
en:
I fled from home at twenty.
And so far I still
live the life of a vagrant.

zh: “长大”是“长大了”，而没有“好”。
en:
True, I've."grown up",
but I'm not yet"all right".

zh: 可是从祖父那里，知道了人生除掉了冰冷和憎恶而外，还有温暖和爱。
en:
Nevertheless, from grandpa
I've learned that
apart from coldness and hatred,
there is also warmth and love in life.

zh: 所以我就向这“温暖”和“爱”的方面，怀着永久的憧憬和追求。
en:
Hence my everlasting dream and pursuit
of this "warmth" and"love".

zh: 你有爱人吗？
en: Don't you have a sweetheart?

zh: 我建议不要带了她去什么名园胜景，还是利用晨昏时节，到深巷中散散步。
en:
Let me suggest that,
instead of accompanying her on a visit to
famous park or scenic spot,
you take her with you for a stroll
in the lane at dawn or dusk.

zh: 在那里，你们俩可以随便谈谈，心贴得更近，
en:
Over there,
you two can chat freely
and with even deeper affection,

zh: 在街上那种贪婪的晚视，恶意的斜觑，巷里是没有的；
en:
free from greedy sidelong glances
or malicious squints
suich as you often
meet with in busy streets.

zh: 偶然呀的一声，墙门口显现出一个人影，又往往是深居简出的姑娘，看见你们，会娇羞地返身回避了。
en:
Suddenly, at a creaking sound,
there may appear a figure by a door
—usually an unsophisticated young girl.
She will, at the sight of you,
withdraw coyly into the house.

zh: 巷，是人海汹汹中的一道避风塘，给人家带来安全感；
en:
The lane is a safe haven
for those struggling in
the turbulent sea of humans
to enjoy a sense of security.

zh:
是城市喧嚣扰擦中的一带洞天幽境，
胜似皇家的阁道，便于平常百姓徘徊裆祥。
en:
It is a heavenly abode
in the inidst of confusion.
Unlike the erstwhile plank-paved path
used exclusively by the imperial family
for their vehicles to move on smoothly,
the lane is a place for the common people
to roam about leisurely.

zh: 爱逐臭争利，铺锆必较的，请到长街闹市去；
en:
Those who strive after fame and gain,
and haggle over every penny,
please go to the downtown area!

zh: 爱轻嘴薄舌的，争是论非的，请到茶馆酒楼去（即茶馆和饭店）;
en:
Those who are sharp-tongued and quarrelsome,
please go to the tea house or restaurant!

zh: 爱锣鼓征锉，管弦嗽嘈的，请到歌台剧院去；
en:
Those who love deafening gongs and drums
as well as noisy wind and string instruments,
please go to the opera house or theatre!

zh: 爱宁静淡泊，沉思默想的，深深的小巷在欢迎你。
en:
Those who are given to
profound meditation
and a quiet life without worldly desires,
welcome to the lane!

zh: 巷 柯灵
en: The Lane Ke Ling

zh: 巷，是城市建筑艺术中一篇飘逸恬静的散文，一幅古雅冲淡的图画。
en:
The lane,
in terms of the art of urban architecture,
is like a piece of
prose of gentle gracefulness
or a painting of
classic elegance and simplicity.

zh: 这种巷，常在江南的小城市中，有如古代的少女，躲在僻静的深闺，轻易不肯抛头露面。
en:
Often tucked away in a small town
south of the Yangtse River,
the lane,
like a maiden of ancient times
hidden away in a secluded boudoir,
is reluctant to make its appearance in public.

zh: 你要在这种城市里住久了，和它真正成了莫逆，你才有机会看见她，接触到她优娴贞静的风度。
en:
You'll never have an opportunity to see it
and savour its gentle poise
until you have become
truly attached to the small town
living there for a long time.

zh: 它不是乡村的陋巷，潞隘破败，泥泞坎坷，杂草乱生，两旁还排列着错落的粪缸。
en:
The lane has nothing in common with
the mean rural alleys,
which are narrow and low-lying,
muddy and bumpy,
overgrown with wild weeds
and lined here and there with manure vats.

zh: 它不是上海的里弄，鳞次桁比的人家，拥挤得喘不过气；
en:
Nor has it anything in common with
linong (meaning alleys) in Shanghai,
which are literally packed with
dwellings and their residents.

zh: 小贩憧幢来往，黝暗的小门边，不时走出一些汲着拖鞋的女子，头发乱似临风飞舞的秋蓬，眼睛里网满红丝，脸上残留着不调和的隔夜脂粉，颓然地走到老虎灶上去提水。
en:
Over there, you'll see vendors hawking their wares here and there.
From time to time, women are seen emerging
from inside some dingy small gates
and shuffling languidly in their slippers towards a laohuzao,
the shop specializing in selling boiled water,
their hair disheveled like wind-blown withered grass in autumn,
their eyes blood-shot, their faces betraying traces of overnight make-up.

zh: 也不像北地的胡同，满目尘土，风起处刮着弥天的黄沙。
en:
Nor has the lane anything in common with
hutong (also meaning alleys) in north China,
which are dusty on every side
especially when a wind rises.

zh: 这种小巷，隔绝了市廛的红尘，却又不是乡村的风味。
en:
The lane,
though cut off from
the hustle and bustle of busy cities,
does not taste of the countryside at all.

zh: 它又深又长，一个人耐心静静走去，要老半天才走完。
en:
It is long and deep,
so it will take you a long while
to walk patiently and quietly through it
from end to end.

zh: 它又这么曲折，你望前面，好像已经堵塞了，可是走过去，一转弯，依然是巷陌深深，而且更加幽静。
en:
It is also so winding that
it seems to be a blind alley
when you look far ahead,
but if you keep walking
until you take a turning,
you'll find it again lying endless
and still more quiet.

zh: 那里常是寂寂的，寂寂的，
en: There is nothing but stillness there.

zh: 不论什么时候，你向巷中炬去，都如宁静的黄昏，可以清晰地听到自己的足音。
en:
At any hour of day,
you can even distinctly hear
in the dusk-like quiet
your own footsteps.

zh: 不高不矮的围墙挡在两边，斑斑驳驳的苔痕，墙上挂着一串串苍翠欲滴的藤萝，简直像古朴的屏风。
en:
On either side of the lane
stand enclosing walls of medium height,
which, moss-covered
and hung with clusters of fresh green wisteria,
look almost like screens of primitive simplicity.

zh: 墙里常是人家的竹园，修竹森森，天毓细细；
en:
Inside the walls are residents'gardens
with dense groves of tall bamboos
as well as soft sounds of nature.

zh: 春来时还常有几枝娇艳的桃花杏花，媳婷婷婷，从墙头殷勤地摇曳红袖，向行人招手。
en:
In spring, beautiful
peach and apricot blossoms a top the walls,
like graceful girls waving their red sleeves,
will sway hospitably to beckon the pedestrians.|

zh: 走过几家墙门，都是紧紧关着，不见一个人影，因为那都是人家的后门。
en:
You'll find the doors in the walls close shut
without a soul in sight
because they are back doors to some households.

zh: 偶然躺着一只狗，但是决不会对你猜猜地狂吠。
en:
Occasionally,
you may come upon a dog lying there,
which, however,
never gives a bark at you.

zh: 小巷的动人处就是它无比的悠闲。
en: The charm of the lane lies in its absolute serenity.

zh: 无论是谁，只要你到巷里去踯躅一会，你的心情就会如巷尾不波的古井，那是一种和平的静穆，而不是阴森和肃杀。
en:
No matter who you are,
if you loiter around in the lane for a while,
your mind will become
as unruffled as the ancient well
at the end of the lane.
There you will experience
a kind of peaceful calmness
rather than gloomy sternness.

zh: 它闹中取静，别有天地，仍是人间。
en:
There reigns peace and quiet
in the midst of noisy bustle.
It is a world of its own on earth.

zh: 它可能是一条现代的乌衣巷，
en:
It may be a modern version of Wu Yi Xiang,
a special residential area of nobility
in the Jin Dynasty
southeast of today's Nanjing,

zh: 家家有自己的一本哀乐帐，一部兴衰史，可是重门叠户，讳莫如深，
en:
where each family,secluded behind closed doors,
has its own covered-up story of
joys and sorrows, and rise and decline.

zh: 夕阳影里，野花闲草，燕子低飞，寻觅归家。
en:
When the sun is setting,
swallows will fly low
over wild flowers and grass
on their way to their nests.

zh: 只是一片澄明如水的气氛，净化一切，笼罩一切，使人忘忧。
en:
The all-pervading and all-purifying atmosphere
of water-like placidness
makes one forget all cares and worries.

zh: 你是否觉得劳生草草，身心两乏？
en:
Aren't you weighed down with cares
in this life of hard toil
and exhausted physically and mentally?

zh:
我劝你工余之暇，常到小巷里走走，那是最好的将息，
会使你消除疲劳，紧张的心弦得到调整。
en:
I would like to advise you
often to take a walk in the lane
in your off-duty hours.
That is the best way to take a rest.
It will dissipate your fatigue
and relieve your nervous tension.

zh: 你如果有时情绪烦燥，心情怆郁，我劝你到小巷里负手行吟一阵，
en:
(When you are fidgety or depressed,
go to the lane and wander around
reciting or composing poems
with your hands crossed behind your back.

zh: 你一定会豁然开朗，怡然自得，物我两忘。
en:
You will then suddenly fall into a bright mood
and enjoy inner peace,
forgetting both yourself and the external world.

zh: 我从事革命斗争，已经十余年了。
en:
I have been engaged in
the revolutionary struggle
for more than a decade.

zh: 在长期的奋斗中，我一向是过着朴素的生活，从没有奢侈过。
en:
During these long militant years,
I have lived a plain life
with no luxuries to speak of.

zh: 经手的款项，总在数百万元；
en:
Millions of dollars
passed through my hands,

zh: 但为革命而筹集的金钱，是一点一滴地用之于革命事业。
en:
but I always saw to it
that every singly cent of the money
raised for the revolution
was spent for no other purposes.

zh: 这在国民党的伟人们看来，颇似奇迹，或认为夸张；
en:
This may sound like
a miracle or an exaggeration
to Kuomintang VIPs.

zh: 而矜持不苟，舍己为公，却是每个共产党员具备的美德。
en:
Self-discipline and self-sacrifice,
however,
are the virtue characteristic of a communist.

zh: 所以，如果有人问身边有没有一些积蓄，那我可以告诉你一桩趣事：
en:
Therefore, should anyone inquire of me
about my personal savings,
let him read the following amusing episode

zh:
就在我被俘的那一天——一个最不幸的日子，
有两个国民党的兵士，在树林中发现了我，
en:
On the day of my capture
-a most inauspicious day it was-
two Kuomintang soldiers
discovered me in a wood.

zh: 而且猜到我是什么人的时候，他们满肚子热望在我身上搜出一千或八百大洋，或者搜出一些金镯金戒指一类的东西，发个意外之财。
en:
Sizing me up,
they thought they had come upon a windfall
and started making a frantic body search,
hopefully to find on me hundred of silvers dollars
or some jewellery like gold bracelets or rings.

zh: 那知道从我上身摸到下身，从袄领捏到袜底，
en:
They frisked me from top to toe
and passed their hands over everything on me
from the collar of my jacket
to the soles of my socks,

zh: 除了一只时表和一枝自来水笔之外，一个铜板都没有搜出。
en:
but, contrary to their expectation,
they found nothing at all,
not even a single copper,
except a watch and a fountain pen.

zh: 他们于是激怒起来了，猜疑我是把钱藏在那里，不肯拿出来。
en:
They were exasperated,
suspecting that
I had my money hidden somewhere
and refused to give it up.

zh: 他们之中有一个左手拿着一个木柄榴弹，
en:
One of the two men
had in his left hand
a wooden-handled grenade.

zh: 右手拉出榴弹中的引线，双脚拉开一步，作出要抛掷的姿势，用凶恶的眼光钉住我，威吓地吼道：
en:
He pulled out the cord
from inside the wooden handled
and moved his legs one step apart
as if he was about to throw the grenade.
Glowering at me ferociously,
he threatened loudly,

zh: “赶快将钱拿出来，不然就是一炸弹，把你炸死去！”
en: Out with your money quick, or you die!

zh: “哼！不要作出那难看的样子来吧！我确实一个铜板都没有存；想从我这里发洋财，是想错了。”我微笑着淡淡地说。
en:
Hey!I said drily with a faint smile.
"Don't you put on such nasty airs!
True I haven't got a single copper with me.
You're barking up wrong tree
to seek a fortune from me."

zh: “你骗谁！像你当大官的人会没有钱！”拿榴弹的兵士坚不相信。
en:
Shit! Nobody can ever believe
a big shot like you ain't got no money!
the soldier with the grenade
remained wholly incredulous.

zh: “决不会没有钱的，一定是藏在那里，我是老出门的，骗不得我”
en:
No money?
the other soldier joined in.
"Impossible!
It must be hidden somewhere.
No fooling an old hand like me."

zh: 另一个兵士一面说，一面弓着背重来一次将我的衣角裤档过细的捏，总企望着有新的发现。
en:
Meanwhile,
he bent low to pass his hand
again meticulously over
every nook and corner of my clothes
and the crotch of my trousers,
still holding out high hopes
of making a new discovery.

zh: “你们要相信我的话，不要瞎忙吧！我不比你们国民党当官的，个个都有钱，我今天确实是一个铜板也没有，我们革命不是为着发财啦！”我再向他们解释。
en:
You should believe me
and stop messing around!
I explained again.
"Unlike your Kuomintang officials
who're rolling in money,
I'm really penniless.
We join the revolution not for personal gain."

zh: 等他们确知在我身上搜不出什么的时候，也就停手不搜了；
en:
Finally,when they knew for certain that
there was no money on me,
they gave up the body search.

zh: 又在我藏躲地方的周围，低头注目搜寻了一番，也毫无所得，他们是多么地失望呵！
en:
Nevertheless,
they lowered their heads to scan
here and there the place where
I had hidden myself,
but again in vain.
How frustrated they must have felt!

zh:
那个持弹欲放地兵士，也将拉着的引线，仍旧塞进榴弹的木柄里，
转过来抢夺我的表和水笔。
en:
The soldier holding grenade
pushed the cord back
into its wooden handle,
and turned round to
scramble for my watch and fountain pen.

zh: 后彼此说定表和笔卖出钱来平分，才算无话。
en:
The two men, however,
settled their dispute by
agreeing to divide the money equally between them
after selling the spoils.

zh:
他们用怀疑而又惊异的目光，对我自上而下地望了几遍，
就同声命令地说：“走吧！”★同声命令地说：译文中用了“bark”，这个词前面我们见过，说的是“狗叫”专门用“bark”，现在先不讲“bark”一词最初的意为“吠叫”，然后引申出来了“大声喊出，厉声说话”这一层意思，单单来形容这两个作威作福的小兵，似不似真的很嘲讽了~
chorus[ko:ras]vt.合唱；齐声背诵；异口同声地说；
en:
They eyed me up and down
with suspicion and amazement
before barking out in chorus,
"come along!"

zh: 是不是还要问问我家里有没有一些财产？
en:
Dear readers, maybe you wish to know
if I have any private property at home.

zh: 请等一下，让我想一想，啊，记起来了，有的有的，但不算多。
en:
Just a minute! Let me see...
Ah, here it is,
but nothing much though.

zh: 去年暑天我穿的几套旧的汗褂裤，与几双缝上底的线袜，已交给我的妻放在深山坞里保藏着——怕国民党军进攻时，被人抢了去，准备今年暑天拿出来再穿；
en:
I have left with my wife
for safe keeping
a few changes of used underwear
and a few pairs of socks with mended soles,
all of which I used to wear last summer.
She has now put them away
in a remote mountain valley
to prevent them from being stolen
in case of Kuomintang attack,
so that I may wear them again this summer.

zh: 那些就算是我唯一的财产了。但我说出那几件“传世宝”来，岂不要叫那些富翁们齿冷三天？!
en:
These are all the property
I have to my name.
But wouldn't
the declaration of my "family treasures"
make myself an object of lively ridicule
to the rich?

zh: 清贫，洁白朴素的生活，正是我们革命者能够战胜许多困难的地方！
en:
To remain honest though poor,
to live a clean and simple life
——that is what we revolutionaries count on
to over come innumerable difficulties!

zh: 动身访美之前，一位旧时同窗写来航空信，再三托付我为他带几棵生枣核。
en:
Before I set out for the US,
a former schoolmate of mine
wrote me by airmail,
asking me in all earnest to
bring him some raw datestones.

zh: 东西倒不占分量，可是用途却很跃跷。
en:
They were not heavy in weight,
yet I was curious about their use.

zh: 从费城出发前，我们就通了电话。
en:
At Philadelphia,
shortly before starting out
for my friend's place,
I called him up.

zh: 一下车，他已经在站上等了。
en:
So when I got off the train at the destination,
I found him already waiting for me at the station.

zh: 掐指一算，分手快半个世纪了，现在都已是风烛残年。
en:
It was about half a century since we last met,
and we were now both in our declining years.

zh:
拥抱之后，他就殷切地问我“带来了吗？”
我赶快从手提包里掏出那几棵枣核。
en:
After hugging each other,
he asked me eagerly,
"have you brought them with you?"
I immediately fished out
the date stones from my handbag.

zh: 他托在掌心，像比珍珠玛瑙还贵重。
en:
He fondled them in his palm
as if they were something
more valuable than pearls or agates.

zh:
他当年那股调皮劲显然还没改。我问起枣核的用途，
他一面往衣兜里揣，一面故弄玄虚地说：“等会儿你就明白了。”
en:
Obviously he was just as childlike as before,
when I asked about the use of the date stones,
he put them into his pocket
and replied by way of fooling me deliberately,
"You'll understand soon."

zh: 那真是座美丽的山城，汽车开去，一路坡上坡下满是一片嫣红。
en:
It was really a beautiful mountain city.
As we drove on,
an expanse of rich crimson
up and down the slope
came into sight.

zh: 过了几个山均，他朝枫树丛中一座三层小楼指了指说：“诺，到了。”
en:
After passing through several cols,
my friend said pointing to
a three-storied house amidst the maple trees,
"here we are."

zh: 汽车拐进草坪，离车库还有三四米，车库就像认识主人似的自动掀起。
en:
The car turned into a lawn
and when it was three or four meters away
form the garage,
its door automatically opened
as if it recognized its own master.

zh: 朋友有点不好意思地解释说，买这座大房子时，孩子们还上着学，如今都成家立业了。学生物化学的老伴儿在一家研究所里做营养试验。
en:
My friend looked somewhat ill at ease
when he told me this:
At the time he bought this big house,
his children had all been at school.
Now they had their own homes and jobs.
His wife, a biochemist,
was a dietician at a research institute.

zh:
他把我安顿在二楼临湖的一个房间后，就领我去踏访他的后花园。
地方不大，布置得却精致匀称。
en:
After assigning me a room
on the second floor facing a lake,
he showed me around his back garden,
which, though not too big,
was exquisite and nicely arranged.

zh: 我们在靠篱笆（=篱笆边）的一张白色长凳上坐下，他劈头就问我：“觉不觉得这花园有点家乡味道？”
en:
The moment we sat down on a white
close to a hedge,
he asked me,
"Don't you find something here
smacking of our native place in China?"

zh: 经他指点，我留意到台阶两旁是他手栽的两株垂杨柳，草坪中央有个睡莲池。
en:
At this, I noticed a weeping willow,
planted by himself,
on either side of a flight of steps
as well as a water-lily pond
in the middle of the garden.

zh: 他感慨良深地对我说：“栽垂柳的时候，我那个小子才五岁，如今在一条核潜艇上当总机械长了。姑娘在哈佛教书。
en:
He said with deep feeling,
"When I planted the willows,
my son was only five.
Now he serves as head of chief mechanics
in a nuclear submarine.
My daughter teaches at Harvard University.

zh: 也许是没出息，怎么年纪越大，思乡越切。
en:
Maybe I'm a bit too foolish.
How come the older I become,
the more I think of my homeland.

zh: 我想厂甸，想隆福寺。
en: I always think of Changdian and Longfusi.

zh: 这里一过圣诞，我就想旧历年。
en:
Every time Christmas is celebrated here in America,
I think of lunar New year back in China.

zh: 近来，我老是想总布胡同院里那棵枣树。
en:
I can never forget
the date tree in
the courtyard of the house on Zongbu Hutong,

zh: 所以才托你带几棵种籽，(我想）试种一下。”
en:
That's why I've asked you
to bring me some date stones.
I'll try to plant them here.

zh:
接着，他又指着花园一角堆起的一座假山假山石说：“你相信吗？
那是我开车到几十里以外，一块块亲手挑选，论公斤买下，
然后用汽车拉回来的。那是我们家的“北海’。”
en:
Then he said pointing to a jumble of rockery
standing in a corner of the garden,
"Believe it or not, the rocks, hand-picked by me,
were bought by the kilogram.
I drove dozens of kilometers away
to haul them back in my car.
Look, that's Beihai in our home."

zh: 说到这里，我们两人都不约而同地站了起来。沿着草坪旁用卵石铺成的小径，走到“北海”跟前。
en:
Thereupon,
we rose to our feet simultaneously
and walked along a cobbled footpath
beside the lawn
towards the miniature Beihai.

zh: 真是个细心人呢，他在上面还嵌了一所泥制的小凉亭，一座红庙，顶上还有尊白塔。朋友解释说，都从旧金山唐人街买来的。
en:
What a careful man my friend was!
He had had the artificial hill
inlaid with a clay pavilion and a red temple.
with a white pagoda on top.
He said he had bought the decorative objects
from China Town in San Francisco.

zh: 他告诉我，时常在月夜，他同老伴儿并肩坐在这长凳上，追忆起当年在北海泛舟的日子。
en:
He also told me that
on a moonlit night he and his wife
would sit side by side on the bench
recalling how they had used to
go boating on the Beihai Lake.

zh: 睡莲的清香迎风扑来，眼前仿佛就闪出一片荷塘佳色。
en:
Meanwhile,
as I smelled the faint scent of the water-lilies
carried to us by the breeze,
I felt as if
the beautiful scene of a Chinese lotus pond
were flashing past my eyes.

zh: 改了国籍，不等于就改了民族感情，而且没有一个民族像我们这么依恋故土的。
en:
The change of nationality
doesn't mean
the change of national feeling.
No other nation
has such a strong attachment for
the native land as we Chinese.

zh: 我已是一个中年的人。一到中年，就有许多不愉快的现象，眼睛昏花了，记忆力减退了，头发开始秃脱而且变白了，意兴，体力，什么都不如年青的时候，常不禁会感觉到难以名言的寂寞的情味。
en:
I am already a middle-aged man.
At middle age,
I feel sad to find
my eyesight and memory failing,
my hair thinning and graying,
and myself no longer mentally and physically
as fit as when I was young.
I often suffer from a nameless loneliness.

zh: 尤其觉得难堪的是知友的逐渐减少和疏远，缺乏交际上的温暖的慰藉。
en:
The most intolerable of all is
the lack of friendly warmth and comfort
due to the gradual passing away and estrangement
of more and more old pals.

zh:
不消说，相识的人数是随了年龄增加的，一个人年龄越大，走过的地方当过的
职务越多，相识的人理该越增加了。
en:
Needless to say,
the number of acquaintances
increases with one's age.
The older one gets,
the more widely traveled one is
and the more work experience one has,
the more acquaintances one
is supposed to have.

zh: 可是相识的人并不就是朋友。
en: But not all acquaintances are friends.

zh: 我们和许多人相识，或是因了事务关系，或是因了偶然的机缘——如在别人请客的时候同席吃过饭之类。
en:
We come to know many people
either in the way of business
or by mere chance
-say, having been at the same table
at a dinner party.

zh: 见面时点头或握手，有事时走访或通信，口头上彼此也“朋友”，笔头上有时或称“仁兄”，
en:
We may be on nodding or hand-shaking terms,
call each other"friend",
sometimes write to each other with
the salutation of "Dear So-and-So", etc., etc.

zh: 诸如此类，其实只是一种社交上的客套，和“顿首”“百拜”同是仪式的虚伪。
en:
All these are, in fact,
nothing but civilities of social life,
as hypocritical as
the polite formula dunshou (kowtow)
or baibai (a hundred greetings)
used after the signature
in old-fashioned Chinese letter-writing.

zh: 这种交际可以说是社交，和真正的友谊相差似乎很远。
en:
We may call them social intercourse,
but they seem to have very little
in common with genuine friendship.

zh: 真正的朋友，恐怕要算“总角之交”或“竹马之交”了。
en:
Real friendship between two persons
originates perhaps from
the time of life when they were children
playing innocently together.

zh: 在小学和中学的时代容易结成真实的友谊，那时彼此尚不感到生活的压迫，入世未深，打算计较的念头也少，朋友的结成全由于志趣相近或性情适合，
en:
Real friendship is easily formed in
primary or middle school days when,
being socially inexperienced
and free from the burden of life,
you give little thought to
personal gains or losses,
and make friends entirely as a result of
similar tastes and interests
or congenial disposition.

zh: 差不多可以说是“无所为”的，性质比较纯粹。
en:
It is sort of
"friendship for friendship's sake"
and is relatively pure in nature.

zh: 二十岁以后结成的友谊，大概已不免掺有各种各样的颜色分子在内；
en:
Friendship among people in their 20s,
however, is more or less
coloured by personal motives.

zh: 至于三十岁四十岁以后的朋友中间，颜色分子愈多，友谊的真实成分也就不免因而愈少了。
en:
And friendship among
those aged over 30
becomes correspondingly still less pure
as it gets even more coloured.

zh: 这并不一定是“人心不古”，实可以说是人生的悲剧。
en:
Though this is not necessarily due to
"degeneration of public morality",
I do have good reasons
to call it the tragedy of life.

zh:
人到了成年以后，彼此都有生活的重担须负，入世既深，顾忌的方面也自然加
多起来，在交际上不许你不计较，不许你不打算，结果彼此都“勾心斗角”，像七巧板似地只选定了某一方面和对方接合。
en:
People at middle age,
with the heavy burden of life
and much experience in the ways of the world,
have more scruples about this and that,
and can not choose
but become more calculating in social dealings
till they start scheming against each other.
They always keep a wary eye,
as it were,
on each other in their association.

zh: 这样的接合当然是很不坚固的，尤其是现代这样什么都到了尖锐化的时代。
en:
Such association is of course fragile,
especially in this
modern age of prevailing sharp conflicts.

zh: 在我自己的交游中，最值得系念的老是（=总是）一此少年时代以来的朋友。
en:
Of all my friends,
those I have known since child-hood
are most worthy of remembrance.

zh: 这些朋友本来数目就不多，有些住在远地，连相会的机会也不可多得。
en:
They are few in number.
Some of them live far away
and we seldom have an opportunity
to see each other.

zh: 他们有的年龄大过了我，有的小我几岁，都是中年以上的人了，平日各人所走的方向不同。思想趣味境遇也都不免互异（=不同）,大家晤谈（=交流）起来，也常会遇到说不出的隔膜的情形。
en:
Some of them are older than I am,
and some a few years younger.
But all of us are in late mid-life.
Since we have each followed
a different course in life,
our ways of thinking, interests
and circumstances are bound to differ,
and often we lack mutual understanding
somehow or other in our conversation.

zh: 如大家话旧，旧事是彼此共喻的，而且大半都是少年时代的事，
en:
Nevertheless,
when we talk over old times,
we will always agree on things in the past
--mostly about things in our childhood days.

zh: “旧游如梦”，把梦也似的过去的少年时代重提，因谈话的进行，同时会联想起许多当时的事情，许多当时的人的面影，这时好象自己仍回归到少年时代去了。
en:
While we retell the dream-like childhood days
in the course of our conversation,
numerous scenes and persons of bygone days
will unfold again before our eyes,
and we will feel like reliving the old days.

zh: 我常在这种时候感到一种快乐，同时也感到一种伤感，那情形好比老妇人突然在抽屉里或箱子里发见了她盛年时的影片。
en:
Often at this moment,
I'll feel at once happy and sad
--like an old lady
suddenly fishing out from her drawer or chest
a photo of her taken in the bloom of her youth.

zh: 逢到和旧友谈话，就不知不觉（无意识x1)地把话题转到旧事上去，这是我的习惯。
en:
When chatting away with my old friends,
I am in the habit of unwittingly
channeling the topic of conversation
toward things of former days.

zh: 我在这上面无意识（无意识x2)地会感到一种温暖地慰藉。
en:
From that I unknowingly
derive some sort of warm solace.

zh: 可是这些旧友一年比一年减少了，本来只是屈指可数的几个，少去一个是无法弥补的。
en:
But old friends are
dwindling away year by year.
They are originally few in number,
so the disappearance of any of them
is an irreparable loss to me.

zh: 我每当听到一个旧友死去的消息，总要惆怅多时。
en:
The news of any old pal's death
will invariably make me sad
in my heart for a long,long time.

zh: 学校教育给我们的好处不但只是灌输知识，最大的好处恐怕还在给与我们求友的机会上。
en:
The imparting of knowledge
is not the sole advantage of school education.
Its greatest advantage is perhaps
the opportunity it affords us
for making friends.

zh: 这好处我到了离学校以后才知道，
en:
It was not until I had already left school
that I began to realize this advantage.

zh: 这几年来更确切地体会到，深悔当时毫不自觉，马马虎虎地过去了。
en:
And in recent years
I have come to understand it even more deeply.
I much regret having
carelessly frittered away my school days
without making many friends.

zh: 近来每日早晚在路上见到两两三三的携了手或挽了肩膀走着的青年学生，我总艳美他们有朋友之乐，暗暗地要在心中替他们祝福。
en:
Recently, every morning or evening,
whenever I see school kids with satchels
walking in twos and threes,
hand in hand or shoulder to shoulder,
I always envy them for enjoying happy friendship,
and inwardly offer them my best wishes.

zh: 你知道中国最有名的人是谁？
en:
Do you know who is
the most well-known person
in China?

zh: 提起此人，人人皆晓，处处闻名。
en:
The name of this person
is a household word all over the country.

zh:
他姓差，名不多，是各省各县各村人氏。
他姓是差，名为不多，
en:
His name is Cha and his given name, Buduo,
which altogether mean "About the Same".
He is a native of every province,
every country and every village in this country.

zh: 你一定见过他，一定听说过别人谈起他。差不多先生的名字天天挂在大家的口头，因为他是中国全国人的代表。
en:
You must have seen
or heard about this person.
His name is always
on the lips of everybody
because he is representative
of the whole Chinese nation.

zh: 差不多先生的相貌和你和我都差不多。
en:
Mr. Cha Buduo has
the same physiognomy
as you and I.

zh: 他有一双眼睛，但看的不很清楚；他有两只耳朵，但听的不很分明；有鼻子和嘴，但他对于气味和口味都不很讲究。
en:
He has a pair of eyes,
but doesn't see clearly.
He has a pair of ears,
but doesn't hear well.
He has a nose and a mouth,
but lacks a keen sense of smell and taste.

zh: 他的脑子也不小，但他的记性却不很精明，他的思想也不很细密（短句合译）。
en:
His brain is none too small,
but he is weak in memory
and sloppy in thinking.

zh: 他常常说：“凡事只要差不多，就好了。何必太精明呢？”
en:
He often says:
"whatever we do,
it's OK to be just about right.
What's the use of
being precise and accurate:"

zh:
他小的时候，他妈叫他去买红糖，他买了白糖回来。
他妈骂他，他摇摇头说：“红糖白糖不是差不多吗？”★从这里开始，都是在讲差不多先森以前的光辉事迹，故都要用过去时态。
★叫他去买红糖，他买了白糖回来：很明显两句中间有一个转折意味→叫着买红糖，他却买回来了一堆白糖→instead。
红糖和白糖纯粹是按照颜色来的：其中“红糖”准确的说是为“红褐色”→brown sugar。★摇摇头说：两个动作→摇头（shook head)+说（said)。
想象一下，一个几岁的小娃娃，像个大人似的一本正经一边摇头，一边说话的样子是不是有够搞笑~
scolded[skauldid]v.责骂，斥责（scold的过去式和过去分词）;
他在学堂的时候，先生问他：“直隶省的西边是哪一省？”他说是陕西。先生说：“错了。是山西，不是陕西。”他说：“陕西同山西，不是差不多吗？”在学校的时候，有一天他的老师问他，
One day in school, the teacher asked him,
那一个省在河北的西边呢？
"Which province borders Hebei on the west?"
他回答说：“陕西。
He answered,"Shaanxi,"
老师纠正他说：
The teacher corrected him,
“搞错了。是山西，不是陕西。
"You are wrong. It's Shanxi, Not Shaanxi."
他又反驳了：“陕西还是山西
He retorted,"Shaanxi or Shanxi,
不都差不多嘛？”
aren't they about the same?"
en:
One day, when he was a child,
his mother sent him out
to buy her some brown sugar,
but he returned with
some white sugar instead.
As his mother scolded him about it,
he shook his head and said,
"Brown sugar or white sugar,
aren't they about the same?"

zh: 后来他在一个钱铺里做伙计，他也会写，也会算，只是总不会精细。
en:
Later Mr. Cha Buduo
served as an assistant at a money shop.
He could write and calculate all right,
but his mathematics were was often faulty.

zh: 十字常常写成千字，千字常常写成十字。掌柜的生气了，常常骂他。
en:
He would mistake
the Chinese character 十(meaning 10)
for千（meaning 1000) or vice versa.
The shop owner was infuriated
and often took him to task.

zh: 他只是笑嘻嘻地赔小心道：“千字比十字只多一小撇，不是差不多吗？”
en:
But he would only explain apologetically
with a grin,
"The character f differs from 十
in merely having one additional short stroke.
Aren't they about the same?"

zh: 有一天他为了一件要紧的事，要搭火车到上海去。他从从容容地走到火车站，迟了两分钟，火车已经开走了。
en:
One day, he wanted to go to Shanghai
by train on urgent business.
But he arrived at the railway station unhurriedly
only to find the train already gone,
because he was two minutes late.

zh: 他白瞪着眼，望着远远的火车上煤烟，摇摇头道：“只好明天再走了，今天走同明天走，也差不多。可是火车公司未免太认真了。8点30分开，同8点32分开，不是差不多吗？”
en:
He stood /staring helplessly at the smoke
belching from the diminishing train,
and shook his head,
"Well, all I can do is leave tomorrow.
After all, today and tomorrow are about the same.
But isn't the railway taking it too seriously?
What's the difference between
departing at 8:30 and 8:32?"

zh: 他一面说，一面慢慢地走回家，心里总不明白为什么火车不肯等他两分钟。
en:
He walked home slowly
while talking to himself
and kept puzzling over
why the train hadn't waited for him
for two minutes more.

zh: 有一天，他忽然得了急病，赶快叫家人去请东街的汪医生。
en:
One day he suddenly fell ill
and immediately told one of his family
to fetch Dr. Wang of East Street.

zh: 那家人急急忙忙地跑去，一时寻不着东街的汪大夫，却把西街牛医王大夫请来后者（代指家人）
en:
The latter went in hurry,
but couldn't find the physician on East Street.
So he fetched instead
Veterinarian Wang of West Street.

zh:
差不多先生病在床上，知道寻错了人；
但病急了，身上痛苦，心里焦急，等不得了，
en:
Mr. Cha Buduo, lying on his sickbed,
knew that a wrong person had been brought home.
But, what with pain and worry,
he could ill afford to wait any longer.

zh: 心里想道：“好在王大夫同汪大夫也差不多，让他试试看罢。”于是这位牛医王大夫走近床前，用医牛的法子给差不多先生治病。
en:
So he said to himself,
"Luckily, Vet Wang
is about the same as Dr. Wang.
Why not let Vet Wang have a try?"
there-upon,the veterinarian
walked up to his bed
to work on him as if he were a cow.

zh: 不上一点钟，差不多先生就一命鸣呼了。
en:
Consequently,
Mr. Cha Buduo kicked the bucket
before an hour was out.

zh:
差不多先生差不多要死的时候，一口气断断续续地说道：“活人同死人也……差……差不多，……凡事只要……差……差……不多……就……好了，……
何……何……必…太认真呢？”他说完了这句格言，方才绝气了。
en:
When Mr. Cha Buduo
was about to breathe his last,
he uttered intermittently in one breath,
"Live or die, it's about...about...the same...
Whatever we do...it's OK...
to be...just...just about right...
Why...why...take it...so seriously?"
as soon as he finished this pet phrase of his,
he stopped breathing.

zh: 他死后，大家都很称赞差不多先生样样事情看得破，想得通；
en:
After Mr. Cha Buduo death,
people all praised him
for his way of seeing things
and his philosophical approach to life.

zh:
大家都说他一生不肯认真，不肯算账，不肯计较，真是一位有德行的人。
于是大家给他取个死后的法号，叫他做圆通大师。
en:
They say that he
refused to take things seriously all his life
and that he was never calculating
or particular about personal gains or losses.
So they called him a virtuous man
and honored him
with the posthumous reverent title
Master of Easy-Going.

zh:
他的名誉越传越远，越久越大。无数无数的人都学他的榜样。
于是人人都成了一个差不多先生。—然而中国从此就成为一个懒人国了。
en:
His name has spread far and wide
and become more and more
celebrated with the passing of time.
Innumerable people
have come to follow his example,
so that everybody
has become a Mr. Cha Buduo.
But lo, China will hence be
a nation of lazybones!
